Homage to the fearsome one with garlands, having beautiful hair! / Homage to the fearsome one with garlands, having beautiful hair! / Homage to you, rider on the back of an ass! Homage to the remover of all afflictions, who embodies the world!

30.s:
namo 'stu viśveśvari pāhi viśvaṃ niṣūdayārīn dvijadevatānām /
namo 'stu te sarvamayi trinetre namo namaste varade prasīda //
30.d:
नमो ऽस्तु विश्वेश्वरि पाहि विश्वं निषूदयारीन् द्विजदेवतानाम् ।
नमो ऽस्तु ते सर्वमयि त्रिनेत्रे नमो नमस्ते वरदे प्रसीद ॥
30.m: Homage to you, O Mistress of the universe! Protect the universe! Slay the enemies of the twice-born and the gods! / Homage to you, who embody everything, three-eyed one! Homage, homage to you, giver of boons, be gracious!

30.s:
brahmāṇī tvaṃ mṛḍānī varaśikhigamanā śaktihastā kumārī vārāhī tvaṃ suvaktrā khagapatigamanā vaiṣṇavī tvaṃ saśārṅgo /
durdṛśyā nārasiṃhī ghuraghuritaravā tvaṃ tathaindrī savajrā tvaṃ mārī carmamuṇḍāśavagamanaratā yoginī yogasiddhā //
30.d:
ब्रह्माणी त्वं मृडानी वरशिखिगमना शक्तिहस्ता कुमारी वाराही त्वं सुवक्त्रा खगपतिगमना वैष्णवी त्वं सशार्ङ्गो ।
दुर्दृश्या नारसिंही घुरघुरितरवा त्वं तथैन्द्री सवज्रा त्वं मारी चर्ममुण्डाशवगमनरता योगिनी योगसिद्धा ॥
30.m: You are Brahmāṇī, you are Mṛḍānī; Kumārī riding the excellent peacock, holding the spear; you are Vārāhī with a fair face; you are Vaiṣṇavī riding the lord of birds, carrying the Śārṅga bow; / you are the terrible Nārasiṃhī with a deep roaring sound; likewise you are Aindrī with the thunderbolt; you are the pestilential Yoginī, Carmamuṇḍā delighting in walking among corpses, perfected in yoga!

30.s:
namaste trinetre bhagavati tavacaraṇānuṣitā ye aharaharvinataśiraso 'vanatāḥ /
nahi nahi paribhavamastyaśubhaṃ ca stutibalikusumakarāḥ satataṃ ye //
30.d:
नमस्ते त्रिनेत्रे भगवति तवचरणानुषिता ये अहरहर्विनतशिरसो ऽवनताः ।
नहि नहि परिभवमस्त्यशुभं च स्तुतिबलिकुसुमकराः सततं ये ॥
30.m: Homage to you, O three-eyed Goddess! Those who adhere to your feet, bowing their heads in devotion day after day, / and whose hands are always filled with praises, offerings, and flowers, never meet with defeat or misfortune.

30.s:
evaṃ stutā suravaraiḥ suraśatrunāśinī prāha prahasya surasiddhamaharṣivaryān /
prāpto mayād bhutatamo bhavatāṃ prasādāt saṃgrāmamūrdhvi suraśatrujayaḥ pramardāt //
30.d:
एवं स्तुता सुरवरैः सुरशत्रुनाशिनी प्राह प्रहस्य सुरसिद्धमहर्षिवर्यान् ।
प्राप्तो मयाद् भुततमो भवतां प्रसादात् संग्राममूर्ध्वि सुरशत्रुजयः प्रमर्दात् ॥
30.m: Thus praised by the best of the gods, the destroyer of the gods' enemies laughed and said to the excellent gods, Siddhas, and great sages: / “By your grace, the most wondrous victory over the enemy of the gods by crushing them on the battlefield has been attained by me.

30.s:
imāṃ stutiṃ bhaktiparā narottamā bhavadbhiruktāmanukīrttayanti /
duḥsvapnanāśo bhavitā na saṃśayo varastathānyo vriyatāmabhīpsitaḥ //
30.d:
इमां स्तुतिं भक्तिपरा नरोत्तमा भवद्भिरुक्तामनुकीर्त्तयन्ति ।
दुःस्वप्ननाशो भविता न संशयो वरस्तथान्यो व्रियतामभीप्सितः ॥
30.m: When the best of men, devoted in faith, recite this hymn uttered by you, / their bad dreams will undoubtedly be destroyed. Choose also another boon that you desire.”

30.s:
devā ūcuḥ /
yadi varadā bhavatī tridaśānāṃ dvijaśiśugoṣu yatasva hitāya /
punarapi devaripūnaparāṃstvaṃ pradaha hutāśanatulyaśarīre //
30.d:
देवा ऊचुः ।
यदि वरदा भवती त्रिदशानां द्विजशिशुगोषु यतस्व हिताय ।
पुनरपि देवरिपूनपरांस्त्वं प्रदह हुताशनतुल्यशरीरे ॥
30.m: The gods said: / “If you are willing to grant a boon to the thirty [gods], strive for the welfare of the twice-born, children, and cows; / furthermore, burn the other enemies of the gods, O you whose body is like fire!”

30.s:
devyuvāca/ /
bhūyo bhaviṣyāmyasṛgukṣitānanā harānanasvedajalodbhavā surāḥ /
andhāsurasyāpratipoṣaṇe ratā nāmnā prasiddhā bhuvaneṣu carcikā //
30.d:
देव्युवाच। ।
भूयो भविष्याम्यसृगुक्षितानना हराननस्वेदजलोद्भवा सुराः ।
अन्धासुरस्याप्रतिपोषणे रता नाम्ना प्रसिद्धा भुवनेषु चर्चिका ॥
30.m: The Goddess said: / “I shall appear again with a face sprinkled with blood, born from the sweat on Hara's face, O gods; / devoted to starving the asura Andhaka, I will be renowned in the worlds by the name of Carcikā.

30.s:
bhūyo vadhiṣyāmi surārimuttamaṃ saṃbhūya nandasya gṛhe yaśodayā /
taṃ vipracittiṃ lavaṇaṃ tathāparau śumbhaṃ niśumbhaṃ daśanaprahārimī //
30.d:
भूयो वधिष्यामि सुरारिमुत्तमं संभूय नन्दस्य गृहे यशोदया ।
तं विप्रचित्तिं लवणं तथापरौ शुम्भं निशुम्भं दशनप्रहारिमी ॥
30.m: Again, born in the house of Nanda through Yaśodā, I shall slay the foremost enemy of the gods— / that Vipracitti, and Lavaṇa, and also the other two, Śumbha and Niśumbha, striking them with my teeth.

30.s:
bhūyaḥ surāstiṣyayuge nirāśinī nirīkṣya mārī ca gṛhe śatakratoḥ /
saṃbhūya devyāmitasatyadhāmayā surā bhariṣyāmi ca śākambharī vai //
30.d:
भूयः सुरास्तिष्ययुगे निराशिनी निरीक्ष्य मारी च गृहे शतक्रतोः ।
संभूय देव्यामितसत्यधामया सुरा भरिष्यामि च शाकम्भरी वै ॥
30.m: Again, O gods, seeing that in the Kali age the world is foodless and plague-ridden, in the realm of Indra / I shall be born as a goddess of boundless truth and splendor, and I shall sustain the gods as Śākambharī.

30.s:
bhūyo vipakṣakṣapaṇāya devā vindhye bhaviṣyamyṛṣirakṣaṇārtham /
durvṛttaceṣṭān vinihatya daityān bhūyaḥ sameṣyāmi surālayaṃ hi //
30.d:
भूयो विपक्षक्षपणाय देवा विन्ध्ये भविष्यम्यृषिरक्षणार्थम् ।
दुर्वृत्तचेष्टान् विनिहत्य दैत्यान् भूयः समेष्यामि सुरालयं हि ॥
30.m: Again, to destroy adversaries and protect the sages, O gods, I will be born on the Vindhya [mountains]; / having slain the Daityas of wicked deeds, I will surely return again to the abode of the gods.

30.s:
yadāruṇākṣo bhavitā mahāsuraḥ tadā bhaviṣyāmi hitāya devātāḥ /
mahālirūpeṇa vinaṣṭajīvitaṃ kṛtvā samaṣyāmi punastriviṣṭapam //
30.d:
यदारुणाक्षो भविता महासुरः तदा भविष्यामि हिताय देवाताः ।
महालिरूपेण विनष्टजीवितं कृत्वा समष्यामि पुनस्त्रिविष्टपम् ॥
30.m: When the great asura Aruṇākṣa arises, then I will appear for the welfare of the gods; / having deprived him of life in the form of a great bee, I will return once again to heaven.”

30.s:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamuktvā varadā surāṇāṃ kṛtvā praṇāmaṃ divajapuṅgavānām /
visṛjya bhūtāni jagāma devī khaṃ siddhasaṃghairanugamyamānā //
30.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वरदा सुराणां कृत्वा प्रणामं दिवजपुङ्गवानाम् ।
विसृज्य भूतानि जगाम देवी खं सिद्धसंघैरनुगम्यमाना ॥
30.m: Pulastya said: / Having spoken thus, the giver of boons to the gods bowed to the foremost among the heaven-born, / dismissed the spirits, and departed into the sky, accompanied by multitudes of Siddhas.

30.s:
idaṃ purāṇaṃ paramaṃ pavitraṃ devyā jayaṃ maṅgaladāyi puṃsām /
śrotavyametanniyataiḥ sadaiva rakṣoghnametadbhagavānuvāca //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe triṃśodhyāyaḥ
30.d:
इदं पुराणं परमं पवित्रं देव्या जयं मङ्गलदायि पुंसाम् ।
श्रोतव्यमेतन्नियतैः सदैव रक्षोघ्नमेतद्भगवानुवाच ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे त्रिंशोध्यायः
30.m:
This ancient story is supremely pure; it brings victory for the Goddess and bestows auspiciousness on men. / It should always be heard by self-controlled people; the Blessed One said that it destroys demons.

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

31.s:
nārada uvāca /
kathaṃ samahiṣaḥ kroñco bhinnaḥ skandena suvrata /
etanme vistarād brahman kathayasvāmitadyute //
31.d:
नारद उवाच ।
कथं समहिषः क्रोञ्चो भिन्नः स्कन्देन सुव्रत ।
एतन्मे विस्तराद् ब्रह्मन् कथयस्वामितद्युते ॥
31.m: Nārada said: / “How was Mount Krauñca, together with the buffalo, pierced by Skanda, O observer of good vows? / Tell me this in detail, O Brahmin of boundless splendor!”

31.s:
pulasatya uvāca/ /
śṛṇuṣva kathayiṣyāmi kathāṃ puṇyāṃ purātanīm /
yaśovṛddhiṃ kumārasya kārtikeyasya nārada //
31.d:
पुलसत्य उवाच। ।
शृणुष्व कथयिष्यामि कथां पुण्यां पुरातनीम् ।
यशोवृद्धिं कुमारस्य कार्तिकेयस्य नारद ॥
31.m: Pulastya said: / “Listen, I will tell the ancient and meritorious story / that enhances the renown of the youth Kārtikeya, O Nārada.

31.s:
yattatpītaṃ hutāśena skannaṃ śukraṃ pinākinaḥ /
tenākrānto 'bhavad brahman mandatejā hutāśanaḥ //
31.d:
यत्तत्पीतं हुताशेन स्कन्नं शुक्रं पिनाकिनः ।
तेनाक्रान्तो ऽभवद् ब्रह्मन् मन्दतेजा हुताशनः ॥
31.m: When that spilled seed of the wielder of the Pināka bow was swallowed by the Fire, / the Fire became overcome by it, O Brahmin, and his luster diminished.

31.s:
tato jagāma devānāṃ sakāśamamitadyutiḥ /
taiścāpi prahitastūrṇaṃ brahmalokaṃ jagāma ha //
31.d:
ततो जगाम देवानां सकाशममितद्युतिः ।
तैश्चापि प्रहितस्तूर्णं ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम ह ॥
31.m: Then, of boundless brilliance, he went to the presence of the gods; / and sent swiftly by them, he went to Brahmaloka.

31.s:
sa gacchan kuṭulāṃ devīṃ dadarśa pathi pāvakaḥ /
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha kuṭile teja etatsudurddharam //
31.d:
स गच्छन् कुटुलां देवीं ददर्श पथि पावकः ।
तां दृष्ट्वा प्राह कुटिले तेज एतत्सुदुर्द्धरम् ॥
31.m: As he was going, the fire Pāvaka saw the goddess Kuṭilā on the path. / Seeing her, he said: ‘O Kuṭilā, this splendor is very difficult to bear;

31.s:
maheśvareṇa saṃtyaktaṃ nirdahed bhuvanānyapi /
tasmāt pratīccha putro 'yaṃ tava dhanyo bhaviṣyati //
31.d:
महेश्वरेण संत्यक्तं निर्दहेद् भुवनान्यपि ।
तस्मात् प्रतीच्छ पुत्रो ऽयं तव धन्यो भविष्यति ॥
31.m: cast out by Maheśvara, it could burn even the worlds. / Therefore, accept it; this son of yours will be fortunate.’

31.s:
ityagninā sā kuṭilā smṛtvā kvamatamuttamam /
prakṣipasvāmbhasi mama prāha vahniṃ mahāpagā //
31.d:
इत्यग्निना सा कुटिला स्मृत्वा क्वमतमुत्तमम् ।
प्रक्षिपस्वाम्भसि मम प्राह वह्निं महापगा ॥
31.m: Being addressed thus by Fire, Kuṭilā, considering that excellent counsel, / that great river said to the Fire: ‘Cast it into my waters.’

31.s:
tatastvadhārayaddevī śārvaṃ tejastvapūpuṣat /
hutāśano/pi bhagavān kāmacārī paribhraman //
31.d:
ततस्त्वधारयद्देवी शार्वं तेजस्त्वपूपुषत् ।
हुताशनो।पि भगवान् कामचारी परिभ्रमन् ॥
31.m: Then the goddess bore Śarva's splendor and nourished it. / The blessed consumer of oblations too, roaming about freely as he wished,

31.s:
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi dhṛtavān havyabhuk tataḥ /
māṃsamasthīni rudhiraṃ medontraretasī tvacaḥ //
31.d:
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि धृतवान् हव्यभुक् ततः ।
मांसमस्थीनि रुधिरं मेदोन्त्ररेतसी त्वचः ॥
31.m: for five thousand years, the eater of oblations bore [the rest of it]. Then / his flesh, bones, blood, fat, intestines, seed, skin,

31.s:
romaśmaśvrakṣikeśādyāḥ sarve jātā hiraṇmayāḥ /
hiraṇyaretā lokeṣu tena gītaśca pāvakaḥ //
31.d:
रोमश्मश्व्रक्षिकेशाद्याः सर्वे जाता हिरण्मयाः ।
हिरण्यरेता लोकेषु तेन गीतश्च पावकः ॥
31.m: body hair, beard, eyes, hair of the head, and all else became golden; / because of that, Pāvaka is sung in the worlds as Hiraṇyaretas.

31.s:
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi kuṭulā jvalanopamam /
dhārayantī tadā garbhaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sthānamāgatā //
31.d:
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि कुटुला ज्वलनोपमम् ।
धारयन्ती तदा गर्भं ब्रह्मणः स्थानमागता ॥
31.m: For five thousand years Kuṭilā bore that embryo resembling fire, / and then came to the abode of Brahmā.

31.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭāvān padmajanmā saṃtapyantīṃ mahāpagām /
dṛṣṭvā papraccha genāyaṃ tava garbhaḥ samāhitaḥ //
31.d:
तां दृष्टावान् पद्मजन्मा संतप्यन्तीं महापगाम् ।
दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छ गेनायं तव गर्भः समाहितः ॥
31.m: The lotus-born [Brahmā] saw that great river burning in agony, / and seeing her, he asked: ‘By whom has this embryo been placed in you?’

31.s:
sā cāha śaṅkaraṃ yattacchrukraṃ pītaṃ hi vahninā /
tadaśaktena tenādya nikṣiptaṃ mayi sattama //
31.d:
सा चाह शङ्करं यत्तच्छ्रुक्रं पीतं हि वह्निना ।
तदशक्तेन तेनाद्य निक्षिप्तं मयि सत्तम ॥
31.m: And she said: ‘That semen of Śaṅkara which was swallowed by Fire / was deposited today in me by him when he was unable [to bear it], O best of beings.

31.s:
pañjavarṣa sahasrāṇi dhārayantyāḥ pitāmaha /
garbhasya varttate kālo na papāta ca karhicit //
31.d:
पञ्जवर्ष सहस्राणि धारयन्त्याः पितामह ।
गर्भस्य वर्त्तते कालो न पपात च कर्हिचित् ॥
31.m: Five thousand years have passed while I have been carrying it, O Grandfather; / the term of the embryo is long overdue, yet it has never fallen out.’

31.s:
tacchrutvā bhagavānāha gaccha tvamudayaṃ girim /
tatrāsti yojanaśataṃ raudraṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat //
31.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवानाह गच्छ त्वमुदयं गिरिम् ।
तत्रास्ति योजनशतं रौद्रं शरवणं महत् ॥
31.m: Hearing that, the Blessed One said: ‘Go to the mountain of the rising sun; / there lies a great and dreadful forest of reeds covering a hundred yojanas.

31.s:
tatraiva kṣipa suśreṇi vistīrṇe girisānuni /
daśavarṣasahasrānte tato bālo bhaviṣyati //
31.d:
तत्रैव क्षिप सुश्रेणि विस्तीर्णे गिरिसानुनि ।
दशवर्षसहस्रान्ते ततो बालो भविष्यति ॥
31.m:
Right there cast [it], O fair-hipped one, upon the wide mountain ridge;
after ten thousand years, a boy will then be born."

31.s:
sā śrutvā brahmaṇo vākyaṃ rūpiṇī girimāgatā /
āgatya garbhaṃ tatyāja sukhenaivādrinandinī //
31.d:
सा श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणो वाक्यं रूपिणी गिरिमागता ।
आगत्य गर्भं तत्याज सुखेनैवाद्रिनन्दिनी ॥
31.m:
Having heard the word of Brahmā, she assumed a bodily form and came to the mountain;
having arrived, the mountain’s daughter easily gave up the embryo.

31.s:
sā tu saṃtyajya taṃ bālaṃ brahmāṇaṃ sahasāgamat /
āpomayī mantravaśāt saṃjātā-kuṭilā satī //
31.d:
सा तु संत्यज्य तं बालं ब्रह्माणं सहसागमत् ।
आपोमयी मन्त्रवशात् संजाता-कुटिला सती ॥
31.m:
Having abandoned that boy, she immediately went to Brahmā;
by the power of the mantra she turned into water, being the virtuous Kuṭilā.

31.s:
tejasā cāpi śārveṇa raukmaṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat /
tannivāsaratāścānye pādapā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ //
31.d:
तेजसा चापि शार्वेण रौक्मं शरवणं महत् ।
तन्निवासरताश्चान्ये पादपा मृगपक्षिणः ॥
31.m:
And by the splendor of Śiva, that great reed-bed became golden,
as did the trees, beasts, and birds dwelling there with delight.

31.s:
tato daśasu pūrṇeṣu śaraddaśaśateṣvatha /
bālārkadīptiḥ saṃjāto bālaḥ kamalalocanaḥ //
31.d:
ततो दशसु पूर्णेषु शरद्दशशतेष्वथ ।
बालार्कदीप्तिः संजातो बालः कमललोचनः ॥
31.m:
Then, when ten hundred autumns were fully complete,
a boy was born, radiant as the morning sun, with eyes like lotuses.

31.s:
uttānaśāyī bhagavān divye śaravaṇe sthitaḥ /
mukhe 'ṅguṣṭhaṃ samākṣipya ruroda ghanarāḍiva //
31.d:
उत्तानशायी भगवान् दिव्ये शरवणे स्थितः ।
मुखे ऽङ्गुष्ठं समाक्षिप्य रुरोद घनराडिव ॥
31.m:
Lying on his back, the blessed one, staying in the divine reed-bed,
putting his thumb into his mouth, wept like the lord of clouds.

31.s:
etasminnantare devyaḥ kṛttikāḥ ṣaṭ sutejasaḥ /
dadṛśuḥ svecchayā yāntyo bālaṃ śaravaṇe sthitam //
31.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देव्यः कृत्तिकाः षट् सुतेजसः ।
ददृशुः स्वेच्छया यान्त्यो बालं शरवणे स्थितम् ॥
31.m:
At that moment, the six Kṛttikā goddesses of great splendor,
wandering at will, saw the boy situated in the reed-bed.

31.s:
kṛpāyuktāḥ samājagmuḥ yatra skandaḥ sthito 'bhavat /
ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvaṃ tasmai stanye 'bhicukruśuḥ //
31.d:
कृपायुक्ताः समाजग्मुः यत्र स्कन्दः स्थितो ऽभवत् ।
अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वं तस्मै स्तन्ये ऽभिचुक्रुशुः ॥
31.m:
Filled with pity, they approached the place where Skanda was;
"I first! I first!" they cried out to him regarding breast-milk.

31.s:
vivadantīḥ sa tā dṛṣṭāvā ṣaṇmukhaḥ samajāyata /
abībharaṃśca tāḥ sarvāḥ śiśuṃ snehācca kṛttikāḥ //
31.d:
विवदन्तीः स ता दृष्टावा षण्मुखः समजायत ।
अबीभरंश्च ताः सर्वाः शिशुं स्नेहाच्च कृत्तिकाः ॥
31.m:
Seeing them disputing, he became six-faced,
and all those Kṛttikās nurtured the child out of love.

31.s:
bhriyamāmaḥ sa tābhistu bālo vṛddhimagānmune /
kārttikeyeti vikhyāto jātaḥ sa balināṃ varaḥ //
31.d:
भ्रियमामः स ताभिस्तु बालो वृद्धिमगान्मुने ।
कार्त्तिकेयेति विख्यातो जातः स बलिनां वरः ॥
31.m:
Being nurtured by them, O sage, the boy grew;
he became known as Kārttikeya, the foremost among the strong.

31.s:
etasminnantare brahman pāvakaṃ prāha padmajaḥ /
kiyatpramāṇaḥ putraste varttate sāmprataṃ guhaḥ //
31.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्रह्मन् पावकं प्राह पद्मजः ।
कियत्प्रमाणः पुत्रस्ते वर्त्तते साम्प्रतं गुहः ॥
31.m:
In the meantime, O Brahmin, the lotus-born [Brahmā] said to Fire:
"Of what measure is your son Guha now?"

31.s:
sa tadvacanamākarṇya ajānaṃstaṃ harātmajam /
provāca putraṃ deveśa na vedmi katamo guhaḥ //
31.d:
स तद्वचनमाकर्ण्य अजानंस्तं हरात्मजम् ।
प्रोवाच पुत्रं देवेश न वेद्मि कतमो गुहः ॥
31.m:
Hearing his words, not knowing that son of Hara,
he said: "O Lord of gods, I do not know of a son, which [one is] Guha."

31.s:
taṃ prāha bhagavān yattu tejaḥ pītaṃ purā tvayā /
traiyambalaṃ trilokeśa jātaḥ śaravaṇe śiśuḥ //
31.d:
तं प्राह भगवान् यत्तु तेजः पीतं पुरा त्वया ।
त्रैयम्बलं त्रिलोकेश जातः शरवणे शिशुः ॥
31.m:
The blessed one said to him: "The splendor of the Three-Eyed One that was drunk by you of old,
O lord of the three worlds, has become a child born in the reed-bed."

31.s:
śrutvā pitāmahavacaḥ pāvakastvarito 'bhyagāt /
veginaṃ meṣamāruhya kuṭilā taṃ dadarśa ha //
31.d:
श्रुत्वा पितामहवचः पावकस्त्वरितो ऽभ्यगात् ।
वेगिनं मेषमारुह्य कुटिला तं ददर्श ह ॥
31.m:
Hearing the words of the grandfather, Fire departed in haste,
mounting a swift ram; and Kuṭilā saw him.

31.s:
tataḥ papraccha kuṭilā śīghraṃ kva vrajase kave /
so 'bravīt putraduṣṭyarthaṃ jātaṃ śaravaṇe śiśum //
31.d:
ततः पप्रच्छ कुटिला शीघ्रं क्व व्रजसे कवे ।
सो ऽब्रवीत् पुत्रदुष्ट्यर्थं जातं शरवणे शिशुम् ॥
31.m:
Then Kuṭilā asked: "Where are you going so quickly, O wise one?"
He said: "To see my son, the child born in the reed-bed."

31.s:
sābravīt tanayo mahyaṃ mametyāha ca pāvakaḥ /
vivadantau dadarsātha svecchācārī janārdanaḥ //
31.d:
साब्रवीत् तनयो मह्यं ममेत्याह च पावकः ।
विवदन्तौ ददर्साथ स्वेच्छाचारी जनार्दनः ॥
31.m:
She said, "He is my son," and Fire said, "He is mine."
Then Janārdana, wandering at will, saw the two disputing.

31.s:
tau papraccha kimarthaṃ vā vivādamiha cakrathaḥ /
tāvūcatuḥ vutraheto rudraśukrodbhavāya hi //
31.d:
तौ पप्रच्छ किमर्थं वा विवादमिह चक्रथः ।
तावूचतुः वुत्रहेतो रुद्रशुक्रोद्भवाय हि ॥
31.m:
He asked the two: "For what reason are you two arguing here?"
The two said: "For the sake of the son born from the seed of Rudra."

31.s:
tāvuvāca harirdevo gaccha taṃ tripurāntakam /
sa yadā vakṣyati deveśastatkurudhvamasaṃśayam //
31.d:
तावुवाच हरिर्देवो गच्छ तं त्रिपुरान्तकम् ।
स यदा वक्ष्यति देवेशस्तत्कुरुध्वमसंशयम् ॥
31.m:
Lord Hari said to the two: "Go to the destroyer of Tripura;
whatever that lord of gods shall say, do that without a doubt."

31.s:
ityuktau vāsudevena kuṭilāgnī harāntikam /
sambhyetyocatustathyaṃ kasya putreti nārada //
31.d:
इत्युक्तौ वासुदेवेन कुटिलाग्नी हरान्तिकम् ।
सम्भ्येत्योचतुस्तथ्यं कस्य पुत्रेति नारद ॥
31.m:
Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, Kuṭilā and Fire, having approached Hara,
said truly: "Whose son is he, O Nārada?"

31.s:
rudrastadvākyamākarṇya harṣanirbharamānasaḥ /
diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti girijāṃ prodbhūtapulako 'bravīt //
31.d:
रुद्रस्तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य हर्षनिर्भरमानसः ।
दिष्ट्या दिष्ट्येति गिरिजां प्रोद्भूतपुलको ऽब्रवीत् ॥
31.m:
Rudra, hearing their words, his mind brimming with joy,
with bristling hair, said to the mountain's daughter: "By good fortune! By good fortune!"

31.s:
tato 'mbikā prāha haraṃ deva gacchāma śiśum /
praṣṭuṃ samāśrayed yaṃ sa tasya putro bhaviṣyati //
31.d:
ततो ऽम्बिका प्राह हरं देव गच्छाम शिशुम् ।
प्रष्टुं समाश्रयेद् यं स तस्य पुत्रो भविष्यति ॥
31.m:
Then Ambikā said to Hara: "O Lord, let us go to the child
to ask: Whomever he resorts to, he shall be the son of that one."

31.s:
bāḍhamityeva bhagavān samuttasthau vṛṣadhvajaḥ /
sahomayā kuṭilayā pāvakena ca dhīmatā //
31.d:
बाढमित्येव भगवान् समुत्तस्थौ वृषध्वजः ।
सहोमया कुटिलया पावकेन च धीमता ॥
31.m:
"So be it," said the blessed bull-bannered Lord, and set out
together with Umā, Kuṭilā, and the wise Fire.

31.s:
saṃprāptāste śaravaṇaṃ harāgnikuṭilāmbikāḥ /
dadṛśuḥ śiśukaṃ taṃ ca kṛttikotsaṅgaśāyinam //
31.d:
संप्राप्तास्ते शरवणं हराग्निकुटिलाम्बिकाः ।
ददृशुः शिशुकं तं च कृत्तिकोत्सङ्गशायिनम् ॥
31.m:
Arrived at the reed-bed, Hara, Fire, Kuṭilā, and Ambikā
saw that little child lying in the lap of the Kṛttikās.

31.s:
tataḥ sa bālakasteṣāṃ matvā cintitamādarāt /
yogī caturmūrtirabhūt ṣaṇmukhaḥ sa śiśustvapi //
31.d:
ततः स बालकस्तेषां मत्वा चिन्तितमादरात् ।
योगी चतुर्मूर्तिरभूत् षण्मुखः स शिशुस्त्वपि ॥
31.m:
Then that boy, respectfully perceiving their thought,
that yogin child, though six-faced, assumed four forms.

31.s:
kumāraḥ śaṅkaramagād viśākho gaurimāgamat /
kuṭilāmagamacchākho mahāseno 'gnimabhyayāt //
31.d:
कुमारः शङ्करमगाद् विशाखो गौरिमागमत् ।
कुटिलामगमच्छाखो महासेनो ऽग्निमभ्ययात् ॥
31.m:
Kumāra went to Śaṅkara; Viśākha went to Gaurī;
Śākha went to Kuṭilā; and Mahāsena approached Fire.

31.s:
tataḥ prītiyuto rudra umā ca kuṭilā tathā /
pāvakaścāpi deveśaḥ parāṃ mudamavāpa ca //
31.d:
ततः प्रीतियुतो रुद्र उमा च कुटिला तथा ।
पावकश्चापि देवेशः परां मुदमवाप च ॥
31.m:
Then Rudra, filled with affection, and Umā, and likewise Kuṭilā,
and Fire, the lord of gods, attained the highest joy.

31.s:
tato 'bruvan kṛttikāstāḥ ṣaṇmukhaḥ kiṃ harātmajaḥ /
tā abravīddharaḥ pratītyā vidhivad vacanaṃ mune //
31.d:
ततो ऽब्रुवन् कृत्तिकास्ताः षण्मुखः किं हरात्मजः ।
ता अब्रवीद्धरः प्रतीत्या विधिवद् वचनं मुने ॥
31.m:
Then those Kṛttikās said: "Is the six-faced one the son of Hara?"
Hara, with conviction, spoke words to them according to rule, O sage:

31.s:
nāmnā tu kārttikeyo hi yuṣmākaṃ tanayastvasau /
kuṭulāyāḥ kumāreti putro 'yaṃ bhavitāvyayaḥ //
31.d:
नाम्ना तु कार्त्तिकेयो हि युष्माकं तनयस्त्वसौ ।
कुटुलायाः कुमारेति पुत्रो ऽयं भविताव्ययः ॥
31.m:
"By the name Kārttikeya, indeed, this one shall be your son;
and as Kumāra, this imperishable one shall be the son of Kuṭilā.

31.s:
skanda ityeva vikhyāto gaurīputro bhavatvasau /
guha ityeva nāmnā ca mamāsau tanayaḥ smṛtaḥ //
31.d:
स्कन्द इत्येव विख्यातो गौरीपुत्रो भवत्वसौ ।
गुह इत्येव नाम्ना च ममासौ तनयः स्मृतः ॥
31.m:
Known as Skanda, let this one be the son of Gaurī;
and by the name Guha, he is considered my son.

31.s: māhāsena iti khyāto hutāśasyāstu putrakaḥ śāradvata iti khyātaḥ sutaḥ śaravaṇasya ca //
31.d: माहासेन इति ख्यातो हुताशस्यास्तु पुत्रकः शारद्वत इति ख्यातः सुतः शरवणस्य च ॥
31.m:
Known as Mahāsena, let him be the son of the Fire-god;
and known as Śāradvata, he is the son of the reed-bed.

31.s:
evameva mahāyogī pṛthivyāṃ khyātimeṣyati /
ṣaḍāsyatvān mahābāhuḥ ṣaṇmukho nāma gīyate //
31.d:
एवमेव महायोगी पृथिव्यां ख्यातिमेष्यति ।
षडास्यत्वान् महाबाहुः षण्मुखो नाम गीयते ॥
31.m:
In this very way the great yogin shall attain renown upon earth;
because of having six faces, the mighty-armed one is sung by the name Ṣaṇmukha."

31.s:
ityevamuktvā bhagavān śūlapāṇiḥ pitāmaham /
sasmāra daivataiḥ sārddha te 'pyājagmustvarānvitāḥ //
31.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा भगवान् शूलपाणिः पितामहम् ।
सस्मार दैवतैः सार्द्ध ते ऽप्याजग्मुस्त्वरान्विताः ॥
31.m:
Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord who holds the trident in his hand
remembered the Grandfather together with the gods; and they too arrived in haste.

31.s:
praṇipatya ca kāmārimumāṃ ca girinandinīm /
dṛṣṭvā hutāśanaṃ prītyā kuṭilāṃ kṛttikāstathā //
31.d:
प्रणिपत्य च कामारिमुमां च गिरिनन्दिनीम् ।
दृष्ट्वा हुताशनं प्रीत्या कुटिलां कृत्तिकास्तथा ॥
31.m:
Bowing to the enemy of Kāma and to Umā, daughter of the mountain,
and looking with joy upon Fire, Kuṭilā, and the Kṛttikās,

31.s: dadṛśurbālamatyugraṃ ṣaṇmukhaṃ sūryasaṃnibham muṣṇantamiva cakṣuṃṣi tejasā svena devatāḥ //
31.d: ददृशुर्बालमत्युग्रं षण्मुखं सूर्यसंनिभम् मुष्णन्तमिव चक्षुंषि तेजसा स्वेन देवताः ॥
31.m:
the deities beheld the fierce, six-faced child, resembling the sun,
as if stealing their eyes with his own splendor.

31.s:
kautukābhivṛtāḥ sarve evamūcuḥ surottamāḥ /
devakāryaṃ tvayā deva kṛtaṃ devyāgninā tathā //
31.d:
कौतुकाभिवृताः सर्वे एवमूचुः सुरोत्तमाः ।
देवकार्यं त्वया देव कृतं देव्याग्निना तथा ॥
31.m:
Filled with wonder, all the foremost gods spoke thus:
"The task of the gods has been accomplished by you, O Lord, and by the goddess, and by Fire.

31.s:
taduttaṣṭha vrajāmo 'dya tīrthamaujasamavyayam /
kurukṣetre sarasvatyāmabhiṣñcāma ṣaṇmukham //
31.d:
तदुत्तष्ठ व्रजामो ऽद्य तीर्थमौजसमव्ययम् ।
कुरुक्षेत्रे सरस्वत्यामभिष्ञ्चाम षण्मुखम् ॥
31.m:
Therefore arise, let us go today to the imperishable tīrtha Ojas;
let us consecrate the six-faced one on the Sarasvatī in Kurukṣetra.

31.s:
senāyāḥ patirastveṣa devagandharvakiṃnarāḥ /
mahiṣaṃ ghātayatveṣa tārakaṃ ca sudāruṇam //
31.d:
सेनायाः पतिरस्त्वेष देवगन्धर्वकिंनराः ।
महिषं घातयत्वेष तारकं च सुदारुणम् ॥
31.m:
Let him be the commander of the army of gods, Gandharvas, and Kiṃnaras;
let him slay Mahiṣa and the exceedingly dreadful Tāraka."

31.s:
bāḍhamityabravīccharvaḥ samuttasthuḥ surāstataḥ /
kumārasahitā jagmuḥ kurukṣetraṃ mahāphalam //
31.d:
बाढमित्यब्रवीच्छर्वः समुत्तस्थुः सुरास्ततः ।
कुमारसहिता जग्मुः कुरुक्षेत्रं महाफलम् ॥
31.m:
"So be it," Śarva said; then the gods arose.
Accompanied by Kumāra, they went to Kurukṣetra, which bestows great fruit.

31.s:
tatraiva devatāḥ sendrā rudrabrahmajanārdanāḥ /
yatnamasyābhiṣekārtaṃ cakrurmunigaṇaiḥ saha //
31.d:
तत्रैव देवताः सेन्द्रा रुद्रब्रह्मजनार्दनाः ।
यत्नमस्याभिषेकार्तं चक्रुर्मुनिगणैः सह ॥
31.m:
Right there the deities, along with Indra, Rudra, Brahmā, and Janārdana,
made preparations for his consecration together with the hosts of sages.

31.s:
tato 'mbunā saptasamudravāhinīnadījalenāpi mahāphalena /
varauṣadhībhiśca sahasramūrttibhistadābhyaṣiñcan gumacyutādyāḥ //
31.d:
ततो ऽम्बुना सप्तसमुद्रवाहिनीनदीजलेनापि महाफलेन ।
वरौषधीभिश्च सहस्रमूर्त्तिभिस्तदाभ्यषिञ्चन् गुमच्युताद्याः ॥
31.m:
Then with water, with the greatly fruitful waters of rivers flowing to the seven seas,
and with excellent medicinal herbs of a thousand forms, Acyuta and the others consecrated Guha.

31.s:
abhiṣiñcati senānyāṃ kumāre divyarūpiṇi /
jagurgandharvapatayo nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ //
31.d:
अभिषिञ्चति सेनान्यां कुमारे दिव्यरूपिणि ।
जगुर्गन्धर्वपतयो ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः ॥
31.m:
As Kumāra of divine form was being consecrated as commander of the army,
the lords of Gandharvas sang and the hosts of Apsarases danced.

31.s:
abhiṣiktaṃ kumāraṃ ca giriputrī nirīkṣya hi /
snehādutsaṅgagaṃ skandaṃ mūrdhnyajighranmurhurmuhuḥ //
31.d:
अभिषिक्तं कुमारं च गिरिपुत्री निरीक्ष्य हि ।
स्नेहादुत्सङ्गगं स्कन्दं मूर्ध्न्यजिघ्रन्मुर्हुर्मुहुः ॥
31.m:
Seeing Kumāra consecrated, the mountain's daughter,
out of love, smelled Skanda who was sitting in her lap on his head again and again.

31.s:
jighratī kārttikeyasya abhiṣekārdramānanam /
bhātyadrijā yathendrasya devamātāditiḥ purā //
31.d:
जिघ्रती कार्त्तिकेयस्य अभिषेकार्द्रमाननम् ।
भात्यद्रिजा यथेन्द्रस्य देवमातादितिः पुरा ॥
31.m:
Smelling the face of Kārttikeya wet with the waters of consecration,
the mountain's daughter shone like Aditi of old, the mother of the gods, smelling Indra's.

31.s:
tadābhiṣiktaṃ tanayaṃ dṛṣṭvā śarvo mudaṃ yayau /
pāvakaḥ kṛttikāścaiva kuṭilā ca yaśasvinī //
31.d:
तदाभिषिक्तं तनयं दृष्ट्वा शर्वो मुदं ययौ ।
पावकः कृत्तिकाश्चैव कुटिला च यशस्विनी ॥
31.m:
Seeing his son consecrated, Śarva then rejoiced,
as did Fire, the Kṛttikās, and the renowned Kuṭilā.

31.s:
tato 'bhiṣiktāsya haraḥ senāpatye guhasya tu /
pramathāṃścaturaḥ pradācchakratulyaparākramān //
31.d:
ततो ऽभिषिक्तास्य हरः सेनापत्ये गुहस्य तु ।
प्रमथांश्चतुरः प्रदाच्छक्रतुल्यपराक्रमान् ॥
31.m:
Then, upon the consecration of Guha to the commandership of the army,
Hara gave four Pramathas equal in prowess to Śakra:

31.s:
ghaṇṭākarṇa lohitākṣaṃ nandisenaṃ ca dāruṇam /
caturthaṃ balināṃ mukhyaṃ khyātaṃ kumudamālinam //
31.d:
घण्टाकर्ण लोहिताक्षं नन्दिसेनं च दारुणम् ।
चतुर्थं बलिनां मुख्यं ख्यातं कुमुदमालिनम् ॥
31.m:
Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Lohitākṣa, the fierce Nandisena,
and the fourth, Kumudamālin, celebrated as foremost among the strong.

31.s:
haradattān gaṇān dṛṣṭvā devāḥ skandasya nārada /
pradaduḥ pramathān svān svān sarve brahmapurogamāḥ //
31.d:
हरदत्तान् गणान् दृष्ट्वा देवाः स्कन्दस्य नारद ।
प्रददुः प्रमथान् स्वान् स्वान् सर्वे ब्रह्मपुरोगमाः ॥
31.m:
Seeing the hosts given by Hara, the gods, O Nārada,
led by Brahmā, all gave their own Pramathas to Skanda.

31.s:
sthāṇuṃ brahma gaṇaṃ prādād viṣṇuḥ prādād gaṇatrayam /
saṃkramaṃ vikramaṃ caiva tṛtīyaṃ ca parākramam //
31.d:
स्थाणुं ब्रह्म गणं प्रादाद् विष्णुः प्रादाद् गणत्रयम् ।
संक्रमं विक्रमं चैव तृतीयं च पराक्रमम् ॥
31.m: Brahmā gave the gaṇa Sthāṇu, and Viṣṇu gave a triad of gaṇas: / Saṃkrama, Vikrama, and the third, Parākrama.

31.s:
utkesaṃ paṅkajaṃ śakro ravirdaṇḍakapiṅgalau /
candro maṇiṃ vasumaṇimaśvinau vatsanandinau //
31.d:
उत्केसं पङ्कजं शक्रो रविर्दण्डकपिङ्गलौ ।
चन्द्रो मणिं वसुमणिमश्विनौ वत्सनन्दिनौ ॥
31.m: Indra gave Utkeśa and Paṅkaja; the Sun gave Daṇḍa and Kapiṅgala; / the Moon gave Maṇi and Vasumaṇi; the Aśvins gave Vatsa and Nandin.

31.s:
jyotirhutāśanaḥ prādājjavalajjihvaṃ tathāparam /
kundaṃ mukundaṃ kusumaṃ trīn dhātānucarān dadau //
31.d:
ज्योतिर्हुताशनः प्रादाज्जवलज्जिह्वं तथापरम् ।
कुन्दं मुकुन्दं कुसुमं त्रीन् धातानुचरान् ददौ ॥
31.m: The fire-god gave Jyotis, and another named Jvalajjihva; / Dhātṛ gave three attendants: Kunda, Mukunda, and Kusuma.

31.s:
cakrānucakrau tvaṣṭāṃ ca vedhātisthirasusthirau /
pāṇityajaṃ kālakañca prādāt pūṣā mahābalau //
31.d:
चक्रानुचक्रौ त्वष्टां च वेधातिस्थिरसुस्थिरौ ।
पाणित्यजं कालकञ्च प्रादात् पूषा महाबलौ ॥
31.m: Tvaṣṭṛ gave Cakra and Anucakra; the Creator [gave] Atisthira and Susthira; / Pūṣan gave two of great strength: Pāṇityaja and Kālaka.

31.s:
svarṇamālaṃ ghanāhvaṃ ca himavān pramathottamau /
prādādevocchrito vindhyastvatiśṛṅgaṃ ca pārṣadam //
31.d:
स्वर्णमालं घनाह्वं च हिमवान् प्रमथोत्तमौ ।
प्रादादेवोच्छ्रितो विन्ध्यस्त्वतिशृङ्गं च पार्षदम् ॥
31.m: Himavat gave two supreme pramathas: Svarṇamāla and the one named Ghana; / and the lofty Vindhya gave an attendant named Atiśṛṅga.

31.s:
suvarcasaṃ ca varuṇaḥ pradadau cātivarcasam /
saṃgrahaṃ vigrahaṃ cābdhirnāgā jayamahājayau //
31.d:
सुवर्चसं च वरुणः प्रददौ चातिवर्चसम् ।
संग्रहं विग्रहं चाब्धिर्नागा जयमहाजयौ ॥
31.m: Varuṇa gave Suvarcas and Ativarcas; / the Ocean gave Saṃgraha and Vigraha; the snakes gave Jaya and Mahājaya.

31.s:
unmādaṃ śuṅkurṇa ca puṣpadantaṃ tathāmbikā /
ghasaṃ cātighasaṃ vāyuḥ prādādanucarāvubhau //
31.d:
उन्मादं शुङ्कुर्ण च पुष्पदन्तं तथाम्बिका ।
घसं चातिघसं वायुः प्रादादनुचरावुभौ ॥
31.m: Ambikā gave Unmāda, Śuṅkarṇa, and Puṣpadanta; / the Wind gave both attendants: Ghasa and Atighasa.

31.s:
parighaṃ caṭakaṃ bhīmaṃ dahatidahanau tathā /
pradadāvaṃśumān pañca pramathān ṣaṇmukhāya hi //
31.d:
परिघं चटकं भीमं दहतिदहनौ तथा ।
प्रददावंशुमान् पञ्च प्रमथान् षण्मुखाय हि ॥
31.m: The Sun gave five pramathas to the six-faced god: / Parigha, Caṭaka, Bhīma, and Dahati and Dahana.

31.s:
yamaḥ pramāthamunmāthaṃ kālasenaṃ mahāmukham /
tālapatraṃ nāḍijaṅghaṃ ṣaḍevānucarān dadau //
31.d:
यमः प्रमाथमुन्माथं कालसेनं महामुखम् ।
तालपत्रं नाडिजङ्घं षडेवानुचरान् ददौ ॥
31.m: Yama gave six attendants: / Pramātha, Unmātha, Kālasena, Mahāmukha, Tālapatra, and Nāḍijaṅgha.

31.s:
suprabhaṃ ca sukarmāṇaṃ dadau dhātā gaṇeśvarau /
suvrataṃ satyasandhaṃ ca mitraḥ pradāda dvijottama //
31.d:
सुप्रभं च सुकर्माणं ददौ धाता गणेश्वरौ ।
सुव्रतं सत्यसन्धं च मित्रः प्रदाद द्विजोत्तम ॥
31.m: Dhātṛ gave two lords of gaṇas: Suprabha and Sukarman; / and Mitra gave Suvrata and Satyasandha, O best of the twice-born.

31.s:
anantaḥ śaṅkupīṭhaśca nikumbhaḥ kumudo 'mbujaḥ /
ekākṣaḥ kunaṭī cakṣuḥ kirīṭī kalaśodaraḥ //
31.d:
अनन्तः शङ्कुपीठश्च निकुम्भः कुमुदो ऽम्बुजः ।
एकाक्षः कुनटी चक्षुः किरीटी कलशोदरः ॥
31.m: Ananta, Śaṅkupīṭha, Nikumbha, Kumuda, Ambuja, / Ekākṣa, Kunaṭī, Cakṣus, Kirīṭin, Kalaśodara,

31.s:
sūcīvaktraḥ kokanadaḥ prahāsaḥ priyako 'cyutaḥ /
gaṇāḥ pañcadaśaite hi yakṣairdattā guhasya tu //
31.d:
सूचीवक्त्रः कोकनदः प्रहासः प्रियको ऽच्युतः ।
गणाः पञ्चदशैते हि यक्षैर्दत्ता गुहस्य तु ॥
31.m: Sūcīvaktra, Kokanada, Prahāsa, Priyaka, and Acyuta— / these fifteen gaṇas were given to Guha by the yakṣas.

31.s:
kālindyāḥ kālakandaśca narmadāyā raṇotkaṭaḥ /
godāvaryāḥ siddhayātrastamasāyādrikampakaḥ /
31.75 sahasrabāhuḥ sītāyā vañjūlāyāḥ sitodaraḥ /
mandākinyāstathā nando vipāśāyāḥ priyaṅkaraḥ //
31.d:
कालिन्द्याः कालकन्दश्च नर्मदाया रणोत्कटः ।
गोदावर्याः सिद्धयात्रस्तमसायाद्रिकम्पकः ।
31.75 सहस्रबाहुः सीताया वञ्जूलायाः सितोदरः ।
मन्दाकिन्यास्तथा नन्दो विपाशायाः प्रियङ्करः ॥
31.m:
Kālakanda of the Kālindī, and Raṇotkaṭa of the Narmadā,
Siddhayātra of the Godāvarī, and Adrikampaka of the Tamasā;

Sahasrabāhu of the Sītā, Sitodara of the Vañjūlā,
and Nanda of the Mandākinī, and Priyaṅkara of the Vipāśā.

31.s:
airāvatyāścaturddaṣṭraḥ ṣoḍaśākṣo vitastayā /
mārjāraṃ sauśikī prādāt krathakrauñcau ca gautamī //
31.d:
ऐरावत्याश्चतुर्द्दष्ट्रः षोडशाक्षो वितस्तया ।
मार्जारं सौशिकी प्रादात् क्रथक्रौञ्चौ च गौतमी ॥
31.m: from Airāvatī, Caturdaṣṭra; by Vitastā, Ṣoḍaśākṣa; / Sauśikī gave Mārjāra; and Gautamī gave Kratha and Krauñca.

31.s:
bāhudā śatasīrṣaṃ ca vāhā gonandanandikau /
bhīmaṃ bhīmarathī prādād vegāriṃ sarayūrdadau //
31.d:
बाहुदा शतसीर्षं च वाहा गोनन्दनन्दिकौ ।
भीमं भीमरथी प्रादाद् वेगारिं सरयूर्ददौ ॥
31.m: Bāhudā gave Śataśīrṣa, and Vāhā gave Gonanda and Nandika; / Bhīmarathī gave Bhīma, and Sarayū gave Vegāri.

31.s:
aṣṭabāhuṃ dadau kāśī subāhumapi gaṇḍakī /
mahānadī citradevaṃ citrā citrarathaṃ dadau //
31.d:
अष्टबाहुं ददौ काशी सुबाहुमपि गण्डकी ।
महानदी चित्रदेवं चित्रा चित्ररथं ददौ ॥
31.m: Kāśī gave Aṣṭabāhu, and Gaṇḍakī gave Subāhu; / Mahānadī gave Citradeva, and Citrā gave Citraratha.

31.s:
kuhūḥ kuvalayaṃ prādānmadhuvarṇaṃ madhūdakā /
jambūkaṃ dhūtapāpā ca veṇā śvetānanaṃ dadau //
31.d:
कुहूः कुवलयं प्रादान्मधुवर्णं मधूदका ।
जम्बूकं धूतपापा च वेणा श्वेताननं ददौ ॥
31.m: Kuhū gave Kuvalaya, and Madhūdakā gave Madhuvarṇa; / Dhūtapāpā gave Jambūka, and Veṇā gave Śvetānana.

31.s:
śrutavarma ca parmāsā revā sāgaraveginam /
prabhāvārthaṃ sahaṃ prādāt kāñcanā kanakekṣaṇam //
31.d:
श्रुतवर्म च पर्मासा रेवा सागरवेगिनम् ।
प्रभावार्थं सहं प्रादात् काञ्चना कनकेक्षणम् ॥
31.m: Parnāsā gave Śrutavarman, and Revā gave Sāgaravegin; / Prabhāvā gave Saha, and Kāñcanā gave Kanakekṣaṇa.

31.s:
gṛdhrapatraṃ ca vimalā cāruvaktraṃ manoharā /
dhūtapāpā mahārāvaṃ karṇā vidrumasaṃnibham //
31.d:
गृध्रपत्रं च विमला चारुवक्त्रं मनोहरा ।
धूतपापा महारावं कर्णा विद्रुमसंनिभम् ॥
31.m: Vimalā gave Gṛdhrapatra, and Manoharā gave Cāruvaktra; / Dhūtapāpā gave Mahārāva, and Karṇā gave one resembling coral.

31.s:
suprasādaṃ suveṇuśca jiṣṇumeghavatī dadau /
yajñabāhuṃ viśālā ca sarasvatyo dadurgaṇān //
31.d:
सुप्रसादं सुवेणुश्च जिष्णुमेघवती ददौ ।
यज्ञबाहुं विशाला च सरस्वत्यो ददुर्गणान् ॥
31.m: Suveṇu gave Suprasāda, and Meghavatī gave Jiṣṇu; / Viśālā and the Sarasvatīs gave Yajñabāhu and gaṇas.

31.s:
kuṭilā tanayasyādāda daśa śakrabalān gaṇān /
karālaṃ sitakeśaṃ ca kṛṣṇakeśaṃ jaṭādharam //
31.d:
कुटिला तनयस्यादाद दश शक्रबलान् गणान् ।
करालं सितकेशं च कृष्णकेशं जटाधरम् ॥
31.m: Kuṭilā gave to her son ten gaṇas with the strength of Indra: / Karāla, Sitakeśa, Kṛṣṇakeśa, Jaṭādhara,

31.s:
meghanādaṃ caturddaṣṭraṃ vidyujihvaṃ daśānanam /
somāpyayanamevograṃ devayājinameva ca //
31.d:
मेघनादं चतुर्द्दष्ट्रं विद्युजिह्वं दशाननम् ।
सोमाप्ययनमेवोग्रं देवयाजिनमेव च ॥
31.m: Meghanāda, Caturdaṣṭra, Vidyujjihva, Daśānana, / Somāpyayana, Ugra, and Devayājin.

31.s:
haṃsāsyaṃ kuṇḍajaṭharaṃ bahugrīvaṃ hayānanam /
kūrmagrīvaṃ ca pañcaitān daduḥ putrāya kṛttikāḥ //
31.d:
हंसास्यं कुण्डजठरं बहुग्रीवं हयाननम् ।
कूर्मग्रीवं च पञ्चैतान् ददुः पुत्राय कृत्तिकाः ॥
31.m: The Kṛttikās gave five to their son: / Haṃsāsya, Kuṇḍajaṭhara, Bahugrīva, Hayānana, and Kūrmagrīva.

31.s:
sthāṇujaṅghaṃ kumbhavaktraṃ lohajaṅghaṃ mahānanam /
piṇḍākāraṃ ca pañacaitān daduḥ skandāyaṭa carṣayaḥ //
31.d:
स्थाणुजङ्घं कुम्भवक्त्रं लोहजङ्घं महाननम् ।
पिण्डाकारं च पञचैतान् ददुः स्कन्दायट चर्षयः ॥
31.m: The sages gave these five to Skanda: / Sthāṇujaṅgha, Kumbhavaktra, Lohajaṅgha, Mahānana, and Piṇḍākāra.

31.s:
nāgajihvaṃ candrabhāsaṃ pāṇikūrmaṃ śaśīkṣakam /
cāṣavaktraṃ ca jambūkaṃ dadau tīrthaḥ pṛthūdakaḥ //
31.d:
नागजिह्वं चन्द्रभासं पाणिकूर्मं शशीक्षकम् ।
चाषवक्त्रं च जम्बूकं ददौ तीर्थः पृथूदकः ॥
31.m: The tīrtha Pṛthūdaka gave Nāgajihva, Candrabhāsa, / Pāṇikūrma, Śaśīkṣaka, Cāṣavaktra, and Jambūka.

31.s:
cakratīrthaṃ sucajakrākṣaṃ makarāśraṃ gayāśiraḥ /
gaṇaṃ pañcaśikhaṃ nāma dadau kanakhalaḥ svakam //
31.d:
चक्रतीर्थं सुचजक्राक्षं मकराश्रं गयाशिरः ।
गणं पञ्चशिखं नाम ददौ कनखलः स्वकम् ॥
31.m: Cakratīrtha gave Sucakrākṣa; Gayāśiras gave Makarāśra; / Kanakhala gave his own gaṇa named Pañcaśikha.

31.s:
bandhudattaṃ vājiśiro bāhuśālaṃ ca puṣkaram /
sarvauñjasaṃ māhiṣakaṃ mānasaḥ piṅgalaṃ yathā //
31.d:
बन्धुदत्तं वाजिशिरो बाहुशालं च पुष्करम् ।
सर्वौञ्जसं माहिषकं मानसः पिङ्गलं यथा ॥
31.m: Puṣkara gave Bandhudatta, Vājiśiras, and Bāhuśāla; / Mānasa likewise gave Sarvojasa, Māhiṣaka, and Piṅgala.

31.s:
rudramauśanasaḥ prādāt tato 'nye mātaro daduḥ /
vasudāmāṃ somatīrthaḥ prabhāso nandinīmapi //
31.d:
रुद्रमौशनसः प्रादात् ततो ऽन्ये मातरो ददुः ।
वसुदामां सोमतीर्थः प्रभासो नन्दिनीमपि ॥
31.m: Auśanasa gave Rudra; then other mothers gave: / Somatīrtha gave Vasudāmā, and Prabhāsa gave Nandinī;

31.s:
indratīrthaṃ viśokāṃ ca udapāno ghanasvanām /
saptasārasvataḥ prādānmātaraścaturodbhutāḥ //
31.d:
इन्द्रतीर्थं विशोकां च उदपानो घनस्वनाम् ।
सप्तसारस्वतः प्रादान्मातरश्चतुरोद्भुताः ॥
31.m: Indratīrtha gave Viśokā, and Udapāna gave Ghanasvanā; / Saptasārasvata gave four wondrous mothers:

31.s:
gītapriyāṃ mādhavīṃ ca tīrthanemiṃ smitānanām /
ekacūḍāṃ nāgatīrthaḥ kurukṣetraṃ palāsadām //
31.d:
गीतप्रियां माधवीं च तीर्थनेमिं स्मिताननाम् ।
एकचूडां नागतीर्थः कुरुक्षेत्रं पलासदाम् ॥
31.m: Gītapriyā, Mādhavī, Tīrthanemi, and Smitānanā; / Nāgatīrtha gave Ekacūḍā, and Kurukṣetra gave Palāsadā;

31.s:
brahmayoniścaṇḍaśilāṃ bhadrakālīṃ triviṣṭapaḥ /
cauṇḍīṃ bhaiṇḍīṃ yogabhaiṇḍīṃ prādāccaraṇapāvanaḥ //
31.d:
ब्रह्मयोनिश्चण्डशिलां भद्रकालीं त्रिविष्टपः ।
चौण्डीं भैण्डीं योगभैण्डीं प्रादाच्चरणपावनः ॥
31.m: Brahmayoni gave Caṇḍaśilā, and Triviṣṭapa gave Bhadrakālī; / Caraṇapāvana gave Cauṇḍī, Bhaiṇḍī, and Yogabhaiṇḍī;

31.s:
sopānīyāṃ mahī prādācchālikāṃ mānaso hradaḥ /
śakaghaṇṭāṃ śatānandāṃ tatholūkhalamekhalām //
31.d:
सोपानीयां मही प्रादाच्छालिकां मानसो ह्रदः ।
शकघण्टां शतानन्दां तथोलूखलमेखलाम् ॥
31.m: the earth gave Sopānīyā, and Lake Mānasa gave Śālikā; / [they also gave] Śakaghaṇṭā, Śatānandā, and Ulūkhalamekhalā.

31.s:
padmāvatī mādhavīṃ ca dadau badarikāśramaḥ /
suṣamāmaikacūḍāṃ ca devīṃ dhamadhamāṃ tathā //
31.d:
पद्मावती माधवीं च ददौ बदरिकाश्रमः ।
सुषमामैकचूडां च देवीं धमधमां तथा ॥
31.m: Badarikāśrama gave Padmāvatī and Mādhavī, / Suṣamā, the goddess Ekacūḍā, and Dhamadhamā.

31.s:
utkrāthanīṃ vedamitrāṃ kedāro mātaro dadau /
sunakṣatrāṃ kadrulāṃ ca suprabhātāṃ muṅgalām //
31.d:
उत्क्राथनीं वेदमित्रां केदारो मातरो ददौ ।
सुनक्षत्रां कद्रुलां च सुप्रभातां मुङ्गलाम् ॥
31.m: Kedāra gave mothers: Utkrāthanī and Vedamitrā, / Sunakṣatrā, Kadrulā, Suprabhātā, and Maṅgalā.

31.s:
devamitrāṃ citrasenāṃ dadau rudramahālayaḥ /
koṭarāmūrdhvaṇīṃ ca śrīmatīṃ bahuputrikām //
31.d:
देवमित्रां चित्रसेनां ददौ रुद्रमहालयः ।
कोटरामूर्ध्वणीं च श्रीमतीं बहुपुत्रिकाम् ॥
31.m: Rudramahālaya gave Devamitrā and Citrasenā, / Koṭarā, Ūrdhvaṇī, the auspicious one, and Bahuputrikā.

31.s:
palitāṃ kamalākṣīṃ ca prayāgo mātaro dadau /
sūpalāṃ madhukumbhāṃ ca khyātiṃ dahadahāṃ parām //
31.d:
पलितां कमलाक्षीं च प्रयागो मातरो ददौ ।
सूपलां मधुकुम्भां च ख्यातिं दहदहां पराम् ॥
31.m: Prayāga gave mothers: Palitā and Kamalākṣī, / Sūpalā, Madhukumbhā, Khyāti, and Dahadahā the supreme.

31.s:
prādāt khaṭakaṭāṃ cānyāṃ sarvapāpavimocanaḥ /
saṃtānikāṃ vikalikāṃ kramaścatvaravāsinīm //
31.d:
प्रादात् खटकटां चान्यां सर्वपापविमोचनः ।
संतानिकां विकलिकां क्रमश्चत्वरवासिनीम् ॥
31.m: Sarvapāpavimocana gave the other one, Khaṭakaṭā, / Saṃtānikā, Vikalikā, and Catvaravāsinī in turn.

31.s:
jaleśvarīṃ kukkuṭikāṃ sudāmāṃ lohamekhalām /
vapuṣmatyutmukākṣī ca kokanāmā mahāśanī /
raudrā karkaṭikā tuṇḍā śvetatīrtho dadau tvimāḥ //
31.d:
जलेश्वरीं कुक्कुटिकां सुदामां लोहमेखलाम् ।
वपुष्मत्युत्मुकाक्षी च कोकनामा महाशनी ।
रौद्रा कर्कटिका तुण्डा श्वेततीर्थो ददौ त्विमाः ॥
31.m: Śvetatīrtha gave these: Jaleśvarī, Kukkuṭikā, Sudāmā, Lohamekhalā, / Vapuṣmatī, Ulmukākṣī, Kokanāmā, Mahāśanī, Raudrā, Karkaṭikā, and Tuṇḍā.

31.s:
etāni bhūtāni gaṇāṃśca mātaro dṛṣṭvā mahātmā vinatātanūjaḥ /
dadau mayūraṃ svasutaṃ mahājavaṃ tathāruṇastāmracūḍaṃ ca putram //
31.d:
एतानि भूतानि गणांश्च मातरो दृष्ट्वा महात्मा विनतातनूजः ।
ददौ मयूरं स्वसुतं महाजवं तथारुणस्ताम्रचूडं च पुत्रम् ॥
31.m: Seeing these spirits, gaṇas, and mothers, the great-souled son of Vinatā / gave his own swift-moving son, the peacock, and Aruṇa gave his son, the rooster.

31.s:
śakti hutāśo 'drisutā ca vastraṃ daṇḍaṃ guruḥ sā kuṭilā kamaṇḍalum /
mālāṃ hariḥ śūladharaḥ patākāṃ kaṇṭhe ca hāraṃ maghavānurastaḥ //
31.d:
शक्ति हुताशो ऽद्रिसुता च वस्त्रं दण्डं गुरुः सा कुटिला कमण्डलुम् ।
मालां हरिः शूलधरः पताकां कण्ठे च हारं मघवानुरस्तः ॥
31.m: The Fire gave a spear, the Mountain's daughter gave garments, the Guru gave a staff, that Kuṭilā gave a water-pot, / Hari gave a garland, the trident-bearer gave a banner, and Indra gave a necklace from his own chest for his neck.

31.s:
gaṇairvṛto mātṛbiranvayāto mayūrasaṃstho varaśaktipāṇiḥ /
sainyādhipatye sa kṛto bhavena rarāja sūryeva mahāvapuṣmān //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ekatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
31.d:
गणैर्वृतो मातृबिरन्वयातो मयूरसंस्थो वरशक्तिपाणिः ।
सैन्याधिपत्ये स कृतो भवेन रराज सूर्येव महावपुष्मान् ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे एकत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
31.m:
Surrounded by gaṇas, followed by the mothers, mounted on the peacock, with the excellent spear in his hand, / having been appointed to command of the army by Bhava, he shone like the sun, possessed of a mighty body.

Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the auspicious Vāmana Purāṇa.

32.s:
pulastya uvāca /
senāpatye 'bhiṣiktastu kumāro daivatairatha /
praṇipatya bhavaṃ bhaktyā girijāṃ pāvakaṃ śucim //
32.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
सेनापत्ये ऽभिषिक्तस्तु कुमारो दैवतैरथ ।
प्रणिपत्य भवं भक्त्या गिरिजां पावकं शुचिम् ॥
32.m: Pulastya said: / Then Kumāra, having been consecrated to the generalship by the gods, / bowed down with devotion before Bhava, the Mountain-born goddess, and the pure Fire,

32.s:
ṣaṭ kṛttikāśca śirasā praṇamya kuṭilāmapi /
brahmāṇaṃ ca namaskṛtya idaṃ vacanamabravīt //
32.d:
षट् कृत्तिकाश्च शिरसा प्रणम्य कुटिलामपि ।
ब्रह्माणं च नमस्कृत्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
32.m: and having bowed his head before the six Kṛttikās and Kuṭilā, / and having paid homage to Brahmā, spoke these words:

32.s:
kumāra uvāca /
namo 'stu bhavatāṃ devā oṃ namo 'stu tapodhanāḥ /
yuṣmatprasādājjeṣyāmi śatrū mahiṣatārakau //
32.d:
कुमार उवाच ।
नमो ऽस्तु भवतां देवा ओं नमो ऽस्तु तपोधनाः ।
युष्मत्प्रसादाज्जेष्यामि शत्रू महिषतारकौ ॥
32.m: Kumāra said: / "Obeisance to you, O gods! Om, obeisance to you, rich in austerity! / By your grace I will conquer the enemies, Mahiṣa and Tāraka."

32.s:
śiśurasmi na jānāmi vaktuṃ kiñcana devatāḥ /
dīyatāṃ brahmaṇā sārddhamanujña mama sāmpratam //
32.d:
शिशुरस्मि न जानामि वक्तुं किञ्चन देवताः ।
दीयतां ब्रह्मणा सार्द्धमनुज्ञ मम साम्प्रतम् ॥
32.m: I am a child, O gods, and know not how to speak at all. / Let permission now be given to me together with Brahmā.

32.s:
ityevamukte vacane kumāreṇa mahātmanā /
mukhaṃ nirīkṣanti surāḥ sreve vigatasādhyamāḥ //
32.d:
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने कुमारेण महात्मना ।
मुखं निरीक्षन्ति सुराः स्रेवे विगतसाध्यमाः ॥
32.m: When these words were thus spoken by the high-souled Kumāra, / all the gods, freed from dismay, gazed at his face.

32.s:
śaṅkaparo 'pi sutasnehāt samutthāya prajāpatim /
ādāya dakṣiṇe pāṇau skandāntikamupāgamat //
32.d:
शङ्कपरो ऽपि सुतस्नेहात् समुत्थाय प्रजापतिम् ।
आदाय दक्षिणे पाणौ स्कन्दान्तिकमुपागमत् ॥
32.m: Śaṅkara too, out of love for his son, rose up, took Prajāpati / by the right hand, and approached Skanda.

32.s:
athomā prāha tanayaṃ putra ehyehi śatruhan /
vandasva caraṇau divyau viṣṇorlokanamaskṛtau //
32.d:
अथोमा प्राह तनयं पुत्र एह्येहि शत्रुहन् ।
वन्दस्व चरणौ दिव्यौ विष्णोर्लोकनमस्कृतौ ॥
32.m: Then Umā said to her son: “Come, come, my son, slayer of foes! / Bow down to the divine feet of Viṣṇu, revered by all the worlds.”

32.s:
tato vihasyāha guhaḥ ko 'yaṃ mātarvadasva mām /
yasyādarāt praṇāmo 'yaṃ kriyate madvidhairjanaiḥ //
32.d:
ततो विहस्याह गुहः को ऽयं मातर्वदस्व माम् ।
यस्यादरात् प्रणामो ऽयं क्रियते मद्विधैर्जनैः ॥
32.m: Then Guha smiled and said: “Tell me, mother, who is this, / to whom people such as I offer such respectful obeisance?”

32.s:
taṃ mātā prāha vacanaṃ kṛte karmaṇi padmabhūḥ /
vakṣyate tava yo 'yaṃ hi mahātmā garuḍadhvajaḥ //
32.d:
तं माता प्राह वचनं कृते कर्मणि पद्मभूः ।
वक्ष्यते तव यो ऽयं हि महात्मा गरुडध्वजः ॥
32.m: His mother addressed him: “When the task is accomplished, the lotus-born [Brahmā] / will explain to you who this great-souled one, whose banner bears Garuḍa, is.

32.s:
kevalaṃ tviha māṃ devastvatpitā prāha śaṅkaraḥ /
nānyaḥ parataro 'smāddhi vayamanye ca dehinaḥ //
32.d:
केवलं त्विह मां देवस्त्वत्पिता प्राह शङ्करः ।
नान्यः परतरो ऽस्माद्धि वयमन्ये च देहिनः ॥
32.m: Only this did the god Śaṅkara, your father, say to me here: / ‘Indeed, none is higher than him; we and the others are embodied beings.’”

32.s:
pārvatyā gadite skandaḥ praṇipatya janārdanam /
tasthau kṛtāñjalipuṭastvājñāṃ prārthayate 'cyutāt //
32.d:
पार्वत्या गदिते स्कन्दः प्रणिपत्य जनार्दनम् ।
तस्थौ कृताञ्जलिपुटस्त्वाज्ञां प्रार्थयते ऽच्युतात् ॥
32.m: Having been told this by Pārvatī, Skanda bowed down to Janārdana / and stood with joined palms, requesting permission from Acyuta.

32.s:
kṛtāñjalipuṭaṃ skandaṃ bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ /
kṛtvā svastyayanaṃ devo hyanujñāṃ pradadau tataḥ //
32.d:
कृताञ्जलिपुटं स्कन्दं भगवान् भूतभावनः ।
कृत्वा स्वस्त्ययनं देवो ह्यनुज्ञां प्रददौ ततः ॥
32.m: To Skanda, who stood with hands folded in reverent greeting, the blessed Lord, the creator of beings, / performed a benediction, and then the god granted permission.

32.s:
nārada uvāca /
yattat svastyayanaṃ puṇyaṃ kṛtavān garuḍadhvajaḥ /
śikhidhvajāya viprarṣe tanme vyākhyātumarhasi //
32.d:
नारद उवाच ।
यत्तत् स्वस्त्ययनं पुण्यं कृतवान् गरुडध्वजः ।
शिखिध्वजाय विप्रर्षे तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
32.m: Nārada said: / That auspicious benediction which he whose banner bears Garuḍa performed / for him whose banner bears a peacock—O Brahmin-seer, you should relate that to me.

32.s:
pulastya uvāca /
śṛṇu svastyayanaṃ puṇyaṃ yatprāha bhagavān hariḥ /
skandasya vijayārthāya mahiṣasya vadhāya ca //
32.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
शृणु स्वस्त्ययनं पुण्यं यत्प्राह भगवान् हरिः ।
स्कन्दस्य विजयार्थाय महिषस्य वधाय च ॥
32.m: Pulastya said: / Listen to the auspicious benediction which the blessed Lord Hari uttered / for the victory of Skanda and for the slaying of Mahiṣa:

32.s:
svasti te kurutāṃ brahma padmayonī rajoguṇaḥ /
svasti cakrāṅkitakaro viṣṇuste vidadhatvājaḥ //
32.d:
स्वस्ति ते कुरुतां ब्रह्म पद्मयोनी रजोगुणः ।
स्वस्ति चक्राङ्कितकरो विष्णुस्ते विदधत्वाजः ॥
32.m: “May Brahmā, lotus-born, of the nature of rajas, grant you well-being; / may the unborn Viṣṇu, whose hand is marked with the discus, grant you well-being.

32.s:
svasti te śaṅkaro bhaktyā sapatnīko vṛṣadhvajaḥ /
pāvakaḥ svasti tubhyaṃ ca karotu śikhivāhana //
32.d:
स्वस्ति ते शङ्करो भक्त्या सपत्नीको वृषध्वजः ।
पावकः स्वस्ति तुभ्यं च करोतु शिखिवाहन ॥
32.m: May Śaṅkara, whose banner bears the bull, together with his consort, lovingly grant you well-being; / and may the Fire-god grant well-being to you, O rider of the peacock!

32.s:
divākaraḥ svasti karotu tubhyaṃ somaḥ sabhaumaḥ sabudho guruśca /
kāvyaḥ sadā svasti karotu tubhyaṃ śanaiścaraḥ svastyayanaṃ karotu //
32.d:
दिवाकरः स्वस्ति करोतु तुभ्यं सोमः सभौमः सबुधो गुरुश्च ।
काव्यः सदा स्वस्ति करोतु तुभ्यं शनैश्चरः स्वस्त्ययनं करोतु ॥
32.m: May the Sun grant you well-being, may the Moon with Mars, with Mercury, and with Jupiter; / may Venus always grant you well-being; may Saturn perform your benediction.

32.s:
marīciratriḥ pulahaḥ pulastyaḥ kraturvasiṣṭho bhṛguraṅgirāśca /
mṛkaṇḍujaste kurutāṃ hi svasti svasti sadā sapta maharṣayaśca //
32.d:
मरीचिरत्रिः पुलहः पुलस्त्यः क्रतुर्वसिष्ठो भृगुरङ्गिराश्च ।
मृकण्डुजस्ते कुरुतां हि स्वस्ति स्वस्ति सदा सप्त महर्षयश्च ॥
32.m: May Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Kratu, Vasiṣṭha, Bhṛgu, and Aṅgiras, / and the son of Mṛkaṇḍu grant you well-being; may the seven great seers always grant you well-being.

32.s:
viśveśvinau sādhyamarudgaṇāgnayo divākarāḥ śūladharā maheśvarāḥ /
yakṣāḥ piśācā vasavo 'tha kinnarāḥ te svasti kurvantu sadodyatāstvamī //
32.d:
विश्वेश्विनौ साध्यमरुद्गणाग्नयो दिवाकराः शूलधरा महेश्वराः ।
यक्षाः पिशाचा वसवो ऽथ किन्नराः ते स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु सदोद्यतास्त्वमी ॥
32.m: May the Viśvedevas, the Aśvins, the Sādhyas, the Maruts, the Fires, the Ādityas, the trident-wielding Maheśvaras, / the Yakṣas, Piśācas, Vasus, and Kinnaras—ever intent, may these grant you well-being.

32.s:
nāgāḥ suparṇāḥ saritaḥ sarāṃsi tīrthāni puṇyāyatanāḥ samudrāḥ /
mahābalā bhūtagaṇā gaṇendrāḥ te svasti kurvantu sadā samudyatāḥ //
32.d:
नागाः सुपर्णाः सरितः सरांसि तीर्थानि पुण्यायतनाः समुद्राः ।
महाबला भूतगणा गणेन्द्राः ते स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु सदा समुद्यताः ॥
32.m: May the Nāgas, the Suparṇas, the rivers, the lakes, the sacred tīrthas, the oceans, / the mighty host of beings, and the lords of the Gaṇas—ever zealous, may they grant you well-being.

32.s:
svasti dvipādikebhyaste catuṣpādebhya eva ca /
svasti te bahupādebhyastvapādebhyo 'pyanāmayam //
32.d:
स्वस्ति द्विपादिकेभ्यस्ते चतुष्पादेभ्य एव च ।
स्वस्ति ते बहुपादेभ्यस्त्वपादेभ्यो ऽप्यनामयम् ॥
32.m: Well-being to you from two-footed creatures, and from four-footed creatures as well; / well-being to you from many-footed ones, and freedom from harm from the footless!

32.s:
prācīṃ dig rakṣatāṃ vajrī dakṣiṇāṃ daṇḍanāyakaḥ /
pāśī pratīcīṃ rakṣatu lakṣmāmaśuḥ pātu cottarām //
32.d:
प्राचीं दिग् रक्षतां वज्री दक्षिणां दण्डनायकः ।
पाशी प्रतीचीं रक्षतु लक्ष्मामशुः पातु चोत्तराम् ॥
32.m: May the wielder of the thunderbolt protect the eastern quarter, the wielder of the rod the southern, / may the wielder of the noose protect the western, and may the deer-marked [Moon] protect the northern.

32.s:
vahnirdakṣimapūrvā ca kubero dakṣiṇāparām /
pratīcīmuttarāṃ vāyuḥ śivaḥ pūrvottarāmapi //
32.d:
वह्निर्दक्षिमपूर्वा च कुबेरो दक्षिणापराम् ।
प्रतीचीमुत्तरां वायुः शिवः पूर्वोत्तरामपि ॥
32.m: May the Fire-god [protect] the south-east, Kubera the south-west, / the Wind-god the north-west, and Śiva the north-east.

32.s:
uvariṣṭād dhruvaḥ śivaḥ purvottarāmapi /
musatī lāṅgalī cakrī dhanuṣmānantareṣu ca //
32.d:
उवरिष्टाद् ध्रुवः शिवः पुर्वोत्तरामपि ।
मुसती लाङ्गली चक्री धनुष्मानन्तरेषु च ॥
32.m: From above, Dhruva and Śiva, and from below as well; / and in the intervals, the wielder of the pestle, the wielder of the plow, the wielder of the discus, and the wielder of the bow.

32.s:
vārāho 'mbunidhau pātu durge pātu nṛkesarī /
sāmavedadhvaniḥ śrīmān sarvalataḥ pātu mādhavaḥ //
32.d:
वाराहो ऽम्बुनिधौ पातु दुर्गे पातु नृकेसरी ।
सामवेदध्वनिः श्रीमान् सर्वलतः पातु माधवः ॥
32.m: May the Boar protect in the ocean, may the Man-Lion protect in impassable places; / may glorious Mādhava, the sound of the Sāmaveda, protect on every side.”

32.s:
pulastya uvāca /
evaṃ kṛtasvastyayano guhaḥ śaktidharo 'graṇīḥ /
praṇipatya surān sarvān samutpatata bhūtalāt //
32.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
एवं कृतस्वस्त्ययनो गुहः शक्तिधरो ऽग्रणीः ।
प्रणिपत्य सुरान् सर्वान् समुत्पतत भूतलात् ॥
32.m: Pulastya said: / Having thus received the benediction, Guha, the spear-bearer and leader, / bowed down to all the gods and soared up from the surface of the earth.

32.s:
tamanveva gaṇāḥ sarve dattā ye muditaiḥ suraiḥ /
anujagmuḥ kumāraṃ te kāmarūpā vihaṅgamāḥ //
32.d:
तमन्वेव गणाः सर्वे दत्ता ये मुदितैः सुरैः ।
अनुजग्मुः कुमारं ते कामरूपा विहङ्गमाः ॥
32.m: Directly after him, all the Gaṇas who were given by the rejoiced gods, / changing their forms at will, flew in pursuit of Kumāra as birds.

32.s:
mātaraśca tathā sarvāḥ samutpeturnabhastalam /
samaṃ skandena balinā hantukāmā mahāsurān //
32.d:
मातरश्च तथा सर्वाः समुत्पेतुर्नभस्तलम् ।
समं स्कन्देन बलिना हन्तुकामा महासुरान् ॥
32.m: And likewise all the Mothers flew up into the vault of heaven / along with the mighty Skanda, desiring to slay the great asuras.

32.s:
tataḥ sudīrghamadhvānaṃ gatvā skando 'bravīd gaṇān /
bhūmyāṃ tūrṇaṃ mahāvīryāḥ kurudhvamavatāraṇam //
32.d:
ततः सुदीर्घमध्वानं गत्वा स्कन्दो ऽब्रवीद् गणान् ।
भूम्यां तूर्णं महावीर्याः कुरुध्वमवतारणम् ॥
32.m: Then, having traversed a very long distance, Skanda said to the Gaṇas: / “O mighty ones, make a swift descent upon the earth!”

32.s:
gaṇā guhavacaḥ śrutvā avatīrya mahītalam /
ārāt patantastaddeśaṃ nādaṃ cakrurbhayaṅkaram //
32.d:
गणा गुहवचः श्रुत्वा अवतीर्य महीतलम् ।
आरात् पतन्तस्तद्देशं नादं चक्रुर्भयङ्करम् ॥
32.m: Hearing Guha’s command, the Gaṇas descended to the surface of the earth, / and alighting near that region, they uttered a terrifying roar.

32.s:
tanninādo mahīṃ sarvāmāpūrya ca nabhastalam /
viveśārṇavarandhreṇa pātālaṃ dānavālayam //
32.d:
तन्निनादो महीं सर्वामापूर्य च नभस्तलम् ।
विवेशार्णवरन्ध्रेण पातालं दानवालयम् ॥
32.m: Filling the entire earth and the vault of heaven, that roar / entered Pātāla, the abode of the Dānavas, through the cleft of the ocean.

32.s:
śrutaḥ sa mahiṣeṇātha tārakema ca dhīmatā /
virojanena jambhena kujambhenāsureṇa ca //
32.d:
श्रुतः स महिषेणाथ तारकेम च धीमता ।
विरोजनेन जम्भेन कुजम्भेनासुरेण च ॥
32.m: It was then heard by Mahiṣa and by the wise Tāraka, / by Virocana, Jambha, and the asura Kujambha.

32.s:
te śrutvā sahasā nādaṃ vajrapātopamaṃ dṛḍham /
kimetaditi saṃcintya tūrṇaṃ jagmustadāndhakam //
32.d:
ते श्रुत्वा सहसा नादं वज्रपातोपमं दृढम् ।
किमेतदिति संचिन्त्य तूर्णं जग्मुस्तदान्धकम् ॥
32.m: Hearing that sudden, tremendous roar resembling the crash of a thunderbolt, / thinking, “What is this?”, they quickly went to Andhaka.

32.s:
te sametyāndhakenaiva samaṃ dānavapuṅgavāḥ /
mantrayāmāsurudvignāstaṃ śabdaṃ prati nārada //
32.d:
ते समेत्यान्धकेनैव समं दानवपुङ्गवाः ।
मन्त्रयामासुरुद्विग्नास्तं शब्दं प्रति नारद ॥
32.m: Having assembled together with Andhaka, those foremost Dānavas, / greatly agitated, took counsel concerning that sound, O Nārada.

32.s:
mantrayatsu ca daityeṣu bhūtalāt sūkarānanaḥ /
pātālaketurdaityendraḥ saṃprāpto 'tha rasātalam //
32.d:
मन्त्रयत्सु च दैत्येषु भूतलात् सूकराननः ।
पातालकेतुर्दैत्येन्द्रः संप्राप्तो ऽथ रसातलम् ॥
32.m: And while the Daityas were deliberating, the boar-faced Daitya lord / Pātālaketu arrived at Rasātala from the surface of the earth.

32.s:
sa bāṇaviddho vyathitaḥ kampamāno muhurmuhuḥ /
abravīd vacanaṃ dīnaṃ samabhyetyāndhakāsuram //
32.d:
स बाणविद्धो व्यथितः कम्पमानो मुहुर्मुहुः ।
अब्रवीद् वचनं दीनं समभ्येत्यान्धकासुरम् ॥
32.m: Pierced by an arrow, tormented, trembling again and again, / he approached the asura Andhaka and spoke these pitiful words:

32.s:
pātālaketuruvāca /
gato 'hamāsaṃ daityendra gālavasyāśramaṃ prati /
taṃ vidhvaṃsayituṃ yatnaṃ samārabdhaṃ balānmayā //
32.d:
पातालकेतुरुवाच ।
गतो ऽहमासं दैत्येन्द्र गालवस्याश्रमं प्रति ।
तं विध्वंसयितुं यत्नं समारब्धं बलान्मया ॥
32.m: Pātālaketu said: / “O Daitya lord, I had gone to the hermitage of Gālava; / an effort was initiated by me to destroy it by force.

32.s:
yāvatsūkarūpeṇa praviśāmi tamāśramam /
na jāne taṃ naraṃ rājan yena me prahitaḥ śaraḥ //
32.d:
यावत्सूकरूपेण प्रविशामि तमाश्रमम् ।
न जाने तं नरं राजन् येन मे प्रहितः शरः ॥
32.m: Just as I entered that hermitage in the form of a boar, / I do not know that man, O king, by whom an arrow was discharged at me.

32.s:
śarasaṃbhinnajatruśca bhayāt tasya mahājavaḥ /
praṇaṣṭa āśramāt tasmāt sa ca māṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt //
32.d:
शरसंभिन्नजत्रुश्च भयात् तस्य महाजवः ।
प्रणष्ट आश्रमात् तस्मात् स च मां पृष्ठतो ऽन्वगात् ॥
32.m: With my collarbone shattered by the arrow, I fled in terror from that hermitage at great speed, / and he pursued me from behind.

32.s:
turaṅgakhuranirghoṣaḥ śrūyate paramo 'sura /
tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vadatastasya śūrasya pṛṣṭhataḥ /
tadbhayādasmi jaladhiṃ saṃprāpto dakṣiṇārṇavam //
32.d:
तुरङ्गखुरनिर्घोषः श्रूयते परमो ऽसुर ।
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति वदतस्तस्य शूरस्य पृष्ठतः ।
तद्भयादस्मि जलधिं संप्राप्तो दक्षिणार्णवम् ॥
32.m: The loud clatter of horse hooves was heard, O asura, / behind that warrior as he cried, ‘Halt, halt!’; / out of fear of him I reached the sea, the southern ocean.

32.s:
yāvatpasyāmi tatrasthān nānāveṣākṛtīn narān /
kecid garjanti ghanavat pratigarjanti cāpare //
32.d:
यावत्पस्यामि तत्रस्थान् नानावेषाकृतीन् नरान् ।
केचिद् गर्जन्ति घनवत् प्रतिगर्जन्ति चापरे ॥
32.m: As soon as I looked, [I saw] men stationed there in various garbs and forms; / some were roaring like clouds, and others roared back.

32.s:
anye cocurvayaṃ nūnaṃ nighnāmo mahiṣāsuram /
tārakaṃ ghātayāmo 'dya vadantyanye sutaijasaḥ //
32.d:
अन्ये चोचुर्वयं नूनं निघ्नामो महिषासुरम् ।
तारकं घातयामो ऽद्य वदन्त्यन्ये सुतैजसः ॥
32.m: Others said: ‘We will surely slay Mahiṣāsura!’ / ‘Today we will kill Tāraka!’, others of supreme splendor were saying.

32.s:
tacchrutvā sutarāṃ trāso mama jāto 'sureśvara /
mahārṇavaṃ parityajya patito 'smi bhayāturaḥ //
32.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा सुतरां त्रासो मम जातो ऽसुरेश्वर ।
महार्णवं परित्यज्य पतितो ऽस्मि भयातुरः ॥
32.m: Hearing that, O lord of asuras, utter terror seized me; / abandoning the great ocean, I fell [into an opening], afflicted by fear.

32.s:
dharaṇyāṃ vivṛtaṃ gartaṃ sa māmanvapatad balī /
tadbhayāt saṃparityajya hiraṇyapuramātmanaḥ //
32.d:
धरण्यां विवृतं गर्तं स मामन्वपतद् बली ।
तद्भयात् संपरित्यज्य हिरण्यपुरमात्मनः ॥
32.m: That mighty one pursued me into a cavity that had opened in the earth; / fleeing in fear of him, abandoning my city of Hiraṇyapura,

32.s:
tavāntikamanuprāptaḥ prasādaṃ kartumarhasi /
tacchratvā cāndhako vākyaṃ prāha meghasvanaṃ vacaḥ //
32.d:
तवान्तिकमनुप्राप्तः प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।
तच्छ्रत्वा चान्धको वाक्यं प्राह मेघस्वनं वचः ॥
32.m: I have come to your presence; please grant me your favor!” / Hearing his words, Andhaka spoke in a voice resonant as a cloud:

32.s:
na bhetavyaṃ tvayā tasmāt satyaṃ goptāsmi dānava /
mahiṣastārakaścobhau bāṇaśca balināṃ varaḥ //
32.d:
न भेतव्यं त्वया तस्मात् सत्यं गोप्तास्मि दानव ।
महिषस्तारकश्चोभौ बाणश्च बलिनां वरः ॥
32.m: “You should not fear him; truly I will protect you, O Dānava! / Both Mahiṣa and Tāraka, and Bāṇa, foremost among the mighty—”

32.s:
anākhyāyaiva te vīrāstvandhakaṃ mahiṣādayaḥ /
svaparigrahasaṃyuktā bhūmiṃ yuddhāya niryayuḥ //
32.d:
अनाख्यायैव ते वीरास्त्वन्धकं महिषादयः ।
स्वपरिग्रहसंयुक्ता भूमिं युद्धाय निर्ययुः ॥
32.m: Without even informing Andhaka, those heroes—Mahiṣa and the others— / marched out to the earth for battle, accompanied by their forces.

32.s:
yatra te dārumākārā gaṇāścakrurmahāsvanam /
tatra daityāḥ samājagmuḥ sāyudhāḥ sabalā mune //
32.d:
यत्र ते दारुमाकारा गणाश्चक्रुर्महास्वनम् ।
तत्र दैत्याः समाजग्मुः सायुधाः सबला मुने ॥
32.m: Where those terrible-looking gaṇas raised a great roar, / there the Daityas arrived, armed and accompanied by their forces, O sage.

32.s:
daityānāpatato dṛṣṭvā kārtikeyagaṇāstataḥ /
abhyadravanta sahasā sa cogro mātṛmaṇḍalaḥ //
32.d:
दैत्यानापततो दृष्ट्वा कार्तिकेयगणास्ततः ।
अभ्यद्रवन्त सहसा स चोग्रो मातृमण्डलः ॥
32.m: Then, seeing the Daityas rushing forward, Kārtikeya's gaṇas, / and that fierce circle of Mothers, rushed toward them with haste.

32.s:
teṣāṃ purassaraḥ sthāṇuḥ pragṛhya parighaṃ balī /
niṣūdayat parabalaṃ kruddho rudraḥ paśūniva //
32.d:
तेषां पुरस्सरः स्थाणुः प्रगृह्य परिघं बली ।
निषूदयत् परबलं क्रुद्धो रुद्रः पशूनिव ॥
32.m: At their head, the mighty Sthāṇu, taking up a club, / slaughtered the enemy army like angry Rudra [slaughtering] beasts.

32.s:
taṃ nighnantaṃ mahādevaṃ nirīkṣya kalaśodaraḥ /
kuṭhāraṃ pāṇinādāya hanti sarvān mahāsurān //
32.d:
तं निघ्नन्तं महादेवं निरीक्ष्य कलशोदरः ।
कुठारं पाणिनादाय हन्ति सर्वान् महासुरान् ॥
32.m: Seeing Mahādeva slaying them, Kalaśodara / took an axe in his hand and struck all the great asuras.

32.s:
jvālāmukho bhayakaraḥ kareṇādāya cāsuram /
sarathaṃ sagajaṃ sāśvaṃ vistṛte vadane 'kṣipata //
32.d:
ज्वालामुखो भयकरः करेणादाय चासुरम् ।
सरथं सगजं साश्वं विस्तृते वदने ऽक्षिपत ॥
32.m: The terrifying Jvālāmukha seized an asura with his hand, / and tossed him with chariot, elephant, and horse into his gaping mouth.

32.s:
daṇḍakaścāpi saṃkruddhaḥ prāsapāṇirmahāsuram /
savāhanaṃ prakṣipati samutpāṭya mahārmave //
32.d:
दण्डकश्चापि संक्रुद्धः प्रासपाणिर्महासुरम् ।
सवाहनं प्रक्षिपति समुत्पाट्य महार्मवे ॥
32.m: The enraged Daṇḍaka, with a spear in his hand, / uprooted a great asura with his mount and hurled him into the great ocean.

32.s:
śaṅkukarṇaśca musalī halenākṛṣya dānavān /
saṃcūrṇayati mantrīva rājānaṃ prāsabhṛd vaśī //
32.d:
शङ्कुकर्णश्च मुसली हलेनाकृष्य दानवान् ।
संचूर्णयति मन्त्रीव राजानं प्रासभृद् वशी ॥
32.m: Śaṅkukarṇa, armed with a mace, dragged the Dānavas with a plow / and crushed them, like a self-controlled minister bearing a spear [crushing] a king.

32.s:
khaḍgacarmadharo vīraḥ puṣpadanto gaṇeśvaraḥ /
dvidhā tridhā ca bahudhā cakre daiteyadānavān //
32.d:
खड्गचर्मधरो वीरः पुष्पदन्तो गणेश्वरः ।
द्विधा त्रिधा च बहुधा चक्रे दैतेयदानवान् ॥
32.m: The heroic Puṣpadanta, a lord of gaṇas bearing sword and shield, / chopped the Daiteyas and Dānavas in two, in three, and into many parts.

32.s:
piṅgalo daṇḍamudyāmya yatra yatra pradhāvati /
tatra tatra pradṛśyante rāśayaḥ śāvadānavaiḥ //
32.d:
पिङ्गलो दण्डमुद्याम्य यत्र यत्र प्रधावति ।
तत्र तत्र प्रदृश्यन्ते राशयः शावदानवैः ॥
32.m: Wherever Piṅgala ran raising his staff, / there piles of corpse-Dānavas were seen.

32.s:
sahasranayanaḥ śūlaṃ bhrāmayan vai gaṇāgraṇīḥ /
nijaghānāsurān vīraḥ savājirathakuñjarān //
32.d:
सहस्रनयनः शूलं भ्रामयन् वै गणाग्रणीः ।
निजघानासुरान् वीरः सवाजिरथकुञ्जरान् ॥
32.m: The heroic leader of gaṇas, Sahasranayana, whirling his trident, / struck down the asuras along with their horses, chariots, and elephants.

32.s:
bhīmo bhīmaśilāvarṣai sa purassarato 'surān /
nijaghāna yathaivendro vajravṛṣṭyā nagottamān //
32.d:
भीमो भीमशिलावर्षै स पुरस्सरतो ऽसुरान् ।
निजघान यथैवेन्द्रो वज्रवृष्ट्या नगोत्तमान् ॥
32.m: Bhīma, at the forefront, slew the asuras with showers of terrible stones, / just as Indra [struck] the greatest mountains with a shower of thunderbolts.

32.s:
raudraḥ śakaṭacakrākṣo gaṇaḥ pañcaśikho balī /
bhrāmayan mudgaraṃ vegānnijaghāna balād ripūn //
32.d:
रौद्रः शकटचक्राक्षो गणः पञ्चशिखो बली ।
भ्रामयन् मुद्गरं वेगान्निजघान बलाद् रिपून् ॥
32.m: The fierce, mighty gaṇa Pañcaśikha, whose eyes were like cartwheels, / swung a mallet with speed and struck down the foes by force.

32.s:
giribhedī talenaiva sārohaṃ kuñjaraṃ raṇe /
bhasma cakre mahāvego rathaṃ ca rathinā saha //
32.d:
गिरिभेदी तलेनैव सारोहं कुञ्जरं रणे ।
भस्म चक्रे महावेगो रथं च रथिना सह ॥
32.m: Giribhedī, of immense speed, with the palm of his hand alone / reduced an elephant with its rider, and a chariot with its warrior, to ashes in battle.

32.s:
nāḍījaṅgho 'ṅghripātaiśca muṣṭibhirjānunāsurān /
kīlabhirvajratulyābhirjaghāna balavān mune //
32.d:
नाडीजङ्घो ऽङ्घ्रिपातैश्च मुष्टिभिर्जानुनासुरान् ।
कीलभिर्वज्रतुल्याभिर्जघान बलवान् मुने ॥
32.m: The powerful Nāḍījaṅgha, O sage, struck the asuras / with kicks, with fists, with his knee, and with bolts like thunderbolts.

32.s:
kūrmagrīvo grīvayaiva śiramā caraṇena ca /
luṇṭhanena tatā daityān nijaghāna savāhanān //
32.d:
कूर्मग्रीवो ग्रीवयैव शिरमा चरणेन च ।
लुण्ठनेन तता दैत्यान् निजघान सवाहनान् ॥
32.m: Kūrmagrīva with his neck, head, and feet, / and by rolling over, slew the Daityas stretched out along with their mounts.

32.s:
piṇḍārakastu tuṇḍena śṛṅgābhyāṃ ca kalipriya /
vidārayati saṃgrāme dānavān samaroddhatān //
32.d:
पिण्डारकस्तु तुण्डेन शृङ्गाभ्यां च कलिप्रिय ।
विदारयति संग्रामे दानवान् समरोद्धतान् ॥
32.m: Piṇḍāraka, who delights in quarrel, with his snout and two horns / tore apart the Dānavas arrogant in battle.

32.s:
tatastatsainyamatulaṃ vadhyamānaṃ gaṇeśvaraiḥ /
pradudrāvātha mahiṣastārakaśca gaṇāgraṇīḥ //
32.d:
ततस्तत्सैन्यमतुलं वध्यमानं गणेश्वरैः ।
प्रदुद्रावाथ महिषस्तारकश्च गणाग्रणीः ॥
32.m: Then, as that matchless army was being slain by the lords of gaṇas, / it fled; and then Mahiṣa and Tāraka, the leaders of the hosts, [stepped forward].

32.s:
te hanyamānāḥ pramathā dānavābhayāṃ varāyudhaiḥ /
parivārya samantāt te yuyudhuḥ kupitāstadā //
32.d:
ते हन्यमानाः प्रमथा दानवाभयां वरायुधैः ।
परिवार्य समन्तात् ते युयुधुः कुपितास्तदा ॥
32.m: Attacked by the two Dānavas with excellent weapons, those pramathas / then surrounded them on all sides and fought in anger.

32.s:
haṃsāsyaḥ paṭṭiśenātha jaghāna mahiṣāsuram /
ṣoṭaśākṣastriśūlena śataśīrṣo varāsinā //
32.d:
हंसास्यः पट्टिशेनाथ जघान महिषासुरम् ।
षोटशाक्षस्त्रिशूलेन शतशीर्षो वरासिना ॥
32.m: Then Haṃsāsya struck the asura Mahiṣa with a paṭṭiśa, / Ṣoḍaśākṣa with a trident, and Śataśīrṣa with an excellent sword.

32.s:
śrutāyudhastu gadayā viśoko musalena tu /
bandhudattastu śūlena mūrdhni daityamatāḍayat //
32.d:
श्रुतायुधस्तु गदया विशोको मुसलेन तु ।
बन्धुदत्तस्तु शूलेन मूर्ध्नि दैत्यमताडयत् ॥
32.m: Śrutāyudha with a mace, Viśoka with a staff, / and Bandhudatta with a spear struck the Daitya upon the head.

32.s:
tathānyaiḥ pārṣadairyuddhe śūlaśaktyṛṣṭipaṭṭiśaiḥ /
nākampat tāḍyamāno 'pi maināka iva parvataḥ //
32.d:
तथान्यैः पार्षदैर्युद्धे शूलशक्त्यृष्टिपट्टिशैः ।
नाकम्पत् ताड्यमानो ऽपि मैनाक इव पर्वतः ॥
32.m: Likewise, struck in battle by other attendants with tridents, spears, lances, and paṭṭiśas, / he did not flinch, like Mount Maināka.

32.s:
tārako bhadrakālyā ca tatholūkhalayā raṇe /
vadhyate caikacūḍāyā dāryate paramāyudhaiḥ //
32.d:
तारको भद्रकाल्या च तथोलूखलया रणे ।
वध्यते चैकचूडाया दार्यते परमायुधैः ॥
32.m: Tāraka was struck in battle by Bhadrakālī and Ulūkhalā, / and was torn by Ekacūḍā with supreme weapons.

32.s:
tau tāḍyamānau pramathairmātṛbhiśca mahāsurau /
na kṣobhaṃ jagmaturvirau kṣobhayantau gaṇānapi //
32.d:
तौ ताड्यमानौ प्रमथैर्मातृभिश्च महासुरौ ।
न क्षोभं जग्मतुर्विरौ क्षोभयन्तौ गणानपि ॥
32.m: Though being beaten by the pramathas and the Mothers, those two heroic great asuras / did not falter, and they agitated the gaṇas.

32.s:
mahiṣo gadayā tūrṇaṃ prahāraiḥ pramathānatha /
parājitya parādhāvat kumāraṃ prati sāyudhaḥ //
32.d:
महिषो गदया तूर्णं प्रहारैः प्रमथानथ ।
पराजित्य पराधावत् कुमारं प्रति सायुधः ॥
32.m: Quickly repelling the pramathas with blows of his mace, / Mahiṣa, weapon in hand, charged toward Kumāra.

32.s:
tamāpatantaṃ mahiṣaṃ sucakrākṣo nirīkṣya hi /
cakramudyamya saṃkruddho rurodha danunandanam //
32.d:
तमापतन्तं महिषं सुचक्राक्षो निरीक्ष्य हि ।
चक्रमुद्यम्य संक्रुद्धो रुरोध दनुनन्दनम् ॥
32.m: Seeing Mahiṣa rushing forward, Sucakrākṣa / raised his discus in fury and blocked the son of Danu.

32.s:
gadācakrāṅkitakarau gaṇāsuramahārathai /
ayudhyetāṃ tada brahman laghu citraṃ ca suṣṭhu ca //
32.d:
गदाचक्राङ्कितकरौ गणासुरमहारथै ।
अयुध्येतां तद ब्रह्मन् लघु चित्रं च सुष्ठु च ॥
32.m: Hands marked by mace and discus, the great chariot-warriors among gaṇas and asuras / fought then, O Brahmin, swiftly, wonderfully, and skillfully.

32.s:
gadāṃ mumoca mahiṣaḥ samāvidhya gaṇāya tu /
sucakrākṣo nijaṃ cakramutsasarjāsuraṃ prati //
32.d:
गदां मुमोच महिषः समाविध्य गणाय तु ।
सुचक्राक्षो निजं चक्रमुत्ससर्जासुरं प्रति ॥
32.m: Mahiṣa swung and hurled his mace at the gaṇa, / while Sucakrākṣa loosed his discus at the asura.

32.s:
gadāṃ chittvā sutīkṣṇāraṃ cakraṃ mahiṣamādravat /
tata uccukruśurdaityā hā hato mahiṣastivati //
32.d:
गदां छित्त्वा सुतीक्ष्णारं चक्रं महिषमाद्रवत् ।
तत उच्चुक्रुशुर्दैत्या हा हतो महिषस्तिवति ॥
32.m: Severing the mace, the discus with exceedingly sharp spokes rushed at Mahiṣa; / then the Daityas cried out: "Alas, Mahiṣa is slain!"

32.s:
tacchrutvābhyadravad bāṇaḥ prāsamāvidhya vegavān /
jaghāna cakraṃ raktākṣaḥ pañjamuṣṭiśatena hi //
32.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वाभ्यद्रवद् बाणः प्रासमाविध्य वेगवान् ।
जघान चक्रं रक्ताक्षः पञ्जमुष्टिशतेन हि ॥
32.m: Hearing that, Bāṇa rushed forward swiftly, brandishing a spear; / the red-eyed one struck the discus with a hundred of his fists.

32.s:
pañcabāhuśatenāpi sucakrākṣaṃ babandha saḥ /
balavānapi bāṇena niṣprayatnagatiḥ kṛtaḥ //
32.d:
पञ्चबाहुशतेनापि सुचक्राक्षं बबन्ध सः ।
बलवानपि बाणेन निष्प्रयत्नगतिः कृतः ॥
32.m: With his five hundred arms, he bound Sucakrākṣa; / though strong, he was rendered motionless by Bāṇa.

32.s:
sucakrākṣaṃ sacakraṃ hi baddhaṃ bāṇāsureṇa hi /
dṛṣṭvādravadgadāpāṇirmakarākṣo mahābalaḥ //
32.d:
सुचक्राक्षं सचक्रं हि बद्धं बाणासुरेण हि ।
दृष्ट्वाद्रवद्गदापाणिर्मकराक्षो महाबलः ॥
32.m: Seeing Sucakrākṣa bound together with his discus by Bāṇāsura, / the mighty Makarākṣa charged with mace in hand.

32.s:
gadayā mūrdhni bāṇaṃ hi nijaghāna mahābalaḥ /
vedanārtto mumocātha sucakrākṣaṃ mahāsuraḥ /
sa cāpi tena saṃyukto vrīḍāyukto mahāmanāḥ //
32.d:
गदया मूर्ध्नि बाणं हि निजघान महाबलः ।
वेदनार्त्तो मुमोचाथ सुचक्राक्षं महासुरः ।
स चापि तेन संयुक्तो व्रीडायुक्तो महामनाः ॥
32.m: The mighty one struck Bāṇa upon the head with his mace; / pained with agony, the great asura released Sucakrākṣa, / and he too, joining [the gaṇas], was high-minded though filled with shame.

32.s:
sa saṃgrāmaṃ parityajya sāligrāmamupāyayau /
bāṇo 'pi makārākṣeṇa tāḍito 'bhūtparāṅmukhaḥ //
32.d:
स संग्रामं परित्यज्य सालिग्राममुपाययौ ।
बाणो ऽपि मकाराक्षेण ताडितो ऽभूत्पराङ्मुखः ॥
32.m: Leaving the battle, he went to Śālagrāma; / and Bāṇa, struck by Makarākṣa, turned his back [and fled].

32.s:
prabhajyata balaṃ sarvaṃ daityānāṃ suratāpasa /
tataḥ svabalamīkṣyaiva prabhagnaṃ tārako balī /
khaḍgodyatakaro daityaḥ pradudrāva gaṇeśvarān //
32.d:
प्रभज्यत बलं सर्वं दैत्यानां सुरतापस ।
ततः स्वबलमीक्ष्यैव प्रभग्नं तारको बली ।
खड्गोद्यतकरो दैत्यः प्रदुद्राव गणेश्वरान् ॥
32.m: The entire army of the Daityas was broken, O ascetic among gods; / then, seeing his own army routed, the mighty Tāraka, / sword raised in hand, ran at the lords of gaṇas.

32.s:
tatastu tenāpratimena sāsinā te haṃsavaktrapramukhā gaṇeśvarāḥ /
samātaraścāpi parājitā raṇe skandaṃ bhayārttāḥ śaraṇaṃ prapedire //
32.d:
ततस्तु तेनाप्रतिमेन सासिना ते हंसवक्त्रप्रमुखा गणेश्वराः ।
समातरश्चापि पराजिता रणे स्कन्दं भयार्त्ताः शरणं प्रपेदिरे ॥
32.m: Then, defeated in battle by that matchless one with his sword, / the lords of gaṇas headed by Haṃsavaktra, along with the Mothers, terrified, sought refuge with Skanda.

32.s:
bhaganān gaṇān vīkṣya maheśvarātmajastaṃ tārakaṃ sāsinamāpatantam /
dṛṣṭvaiva śaktyā hṛdaye bibheda sa bhinnamarmā nyapatat pṛthivyām //
32.d:
भगनान् गणान् वीक्ष्य महेश्वरात्मजस्तं तारकं सासिनमापतन्तम् ।
दृष्ट्वैव शक्त्या हृदये बिभेद स भिन्नमर्मा न्यपतत् पृथिव्याम् ॥
32.m: Seeing the broken gaṇas and seeing Tāraka rushing forward with his sword, / the son of Maheśvara pierced his heart with a spear; his vital spots torn, he fell to the earth.

32.s:
tasminhate bhrātari bhagnadarpo bhayāturo 'bhūnmahiṣo maharṣe /
saṃtyajya saṃgrāmaśiro durātmā jagāma śailaṃ sa dimācalākhyam //
32.d:
तस्मिन्हते भ्रातरि भग्नदर्पो भयातुरो ऽभून्महिषो महर्षे ।
संत्यज्य संग्रामशिरो दुरात्मा जगाम शैलं स दिमाचलाख्यम् ॥
32.m: His brother having been slain, his pride crushed, Mahiṣa was seized with terror, O great sage; / abandoning the forefront of battle, that wicked-souled one went to the mountain called Himācala.

32.s:
bāṇo 'pi vīre nihate 'tha tārake gate himādriṃ mahiṣe bhayātte /
bhayād viveśogramapāṃ nidhānaṃ garṇairbale vadhyati sāparādhe //
32.d:
बाणो ऽपि वीरे निहते ऽथ तारके गते हिमाद्रिं महिषे भयात्ते ।
भयाद् विवेशोग्रमपां निधानं गर्णैर्बले वध्यति सापराधे ॥
32.m: When the heroic Tāraka was slain and Mahiṣa had fled in fear to the Snow Mountain, / Bāṇa also, out of fear, entered the fierce reservoir of water, as the army was being slain by the gaṇas for its offense.

32.s:
hatvā kumāro raṇamurdhni tārakaṃ pragṛhya śaktiṃ mahatā javena /
mayūramāruhya śikhaṇḍamaṇḍitaṃ yayau nihantuṃ mahiṣāsurasya //
32.d:
हत्वा कुमारो रणमुर्ध्नि तारकं प्रगृह्य शक्तिं महता जवेन ।
मयूरमारुह्य शिखण्डमण्डितं ययौ निहन्तुं महिषासुरस्य ॥
32.m: Having slain Tāraka at the head of battle, Kumāra took his spear, / and mounting a peacock adorned with its crest, set out with great speed to kill the asura Mahiṣa.

32.s:
sa pṛṣṭhataḥ prekṣya śikaṇḍiketanaṃ samāpatantaṃ varaśaktipāṇinam /
kailāsamutsṛjya himācalaṃ tathā krauñcaṃ samabhyetva guhaṃ viveśa //
32.d:
स पृष्ठतः प्रेक्ष्य शिकण्डिकेतनं समापतन्तं वरशक्तिपाणिनम् ।
कैलासमुत्सृज्य हिमाचलं तथा क्रौञ्चं समभ्येत्व गुहं विवेश ॥
32.m: Seeing the one with the peacock banner approaching from behind, excellent spear in hand, / [Mahiṣa] abandoned Kailāsa and Himācala, went to Krauñca, and entered a cave.

32.s:
daityaṃ praviṣṭaṃ sa pinākisūnurjugopa yatnād bhagavān suho 'pi /
svabandhuhantā bhavitā kathaṃ tvahaṃ saṃcintayanneva tataḥ sthito 'bhūt //
32.d:
दैत्यं प्रविष्टं स पिनाकिसूनुर्जुगोप यत्नाद् भगवान् सुहो ऽपि ।
स्वबन्धुहन्ता भविता कथं त्वहं संचिन्तयन्नेव ततः स्थितो ऽभूत् ॥
32.m: When the Daitya had entered, the blessed Guha, the son of the bowman [Śiva], guarded [the mountain] with care, / yet stood there reflecting: "How shall I become the slayer of my own kin?"

32.s:
tato 'bhyagāt puṣkarasaṃbhavastu haro murāristridaseśvaraśca /
abhyetya cocurmahiṣaṃ saśailaṃ bhindasva śaktyā kuru devakāryam //
32.d:
ततो ऽभ्यगात् पुष्करसंभवस्तु हरो मुरारिस्त्रिदसेश्वरश्च ।
अभ्येत्य चोचुर्महिषं सशैलं भिन्दस्व शक्त्या कुरु देवकार्यम् ॥
32.m: Then the one born from the lotus [Brahmā], Hara, Murāri, and Indra came; / having approached, they said: "Split Mahiṣa along with the mountain with your spear, and fulfill the purpose of the gods!"

32.s:
tat kārtikeyaḥ priyameva tathyaṃ śrutvā vacaḥ prāha surān vihasya /
kathaṃ hi mātāmahanaptṛkaṃ vadhe svabhrātaraṃ bhrātṛsutaṃ ca mātuḥ //
32.d:
तत् कार्तिकेयः प्रियमेव तथ्यं श्रुत्वा वचः प्राह सुरान् विहस्य ।
कथं हि मातामहनप्तृकं वधे स्वभ्रातरं भ्रातृसुतं च मातुः ॥
32.m: Hearing their pleasing and truthful speech, Kārtikeya smiled and said to the gods: / "How indeed can I slay my maternal grandfather's grandson, my own brother and my mother's brother's son?"

32.s:
eṣā śrutiścāpi purātanī kila gāyanti yāṃ vedavido maharṣayaḥ /
kṛtvā ca yasyā matamuttamāyāḥ svargaṃ vrajanti tvatipāpino 'pi //
32.d:
एषा श्रुतिश्चापि पुरातनी किल गायन्ति यां वेदविदो महर्षयः ।
कृत्वा च यस्या मतमुत्तमायाः स्वर्गं व्रजन्ति त्वतिपापिनो ऽपि ॥
32.m: And this is the ancient scripture which the great seers who know the Vedas sing, / and having followed whose excellent judgment even the worst sinners go to heaven:

32.s:
gāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vṛddhamathāptavākyaṃ bālaṃ svabandhuṃ lalanāmaduṣṭām /
kṛtāparādhā api naiva vadhyā ācāryamukhyā guravastathaiva //
32.d:
गां ब्राह्मणं वृद्धमथाप्तवाक्यं बालं स्वबन्धुं ललनामदुष्टाम् ।
कृतापराधा अपि नैव वध्या आचार्यमुख्या गुरवस्तथैव ॥
32.m: “A cow, a Brahmin, an old person, a trusted speaker, a child, one's own kinsman, an uncorrupted woman, / even if they have committed offenses, must not be killed, and likewise preceptors headed by the teacher.”

32.s:
evaṃ jānan dharmamagryaṃ surendrā nāhaṃ hanyāṃ bhātaraṃ mātuleyam /
yadā daityo nirgāmiṣyad guhāntaḥ tadā śaktyā ghātāyiṣyāmi śatrum //
32.d:
एवं जानन् धर्ममग्र्यं सुरेन्द्रा नाहं हन्यां भातरं मातुलेयम् ।
यदा दैत्यो निर्गामिष्यद् गुहान्तः तदा शक्त्या घातायिष्यामि शत्रुम् ॥
32.m: Knowing thus the supreme dharma, O chiefs of the gods, I will not slay a brother, the son of my maternal uncle. / When the Daitya emerges from within the cave, then I will strike the enemy down with my spear.

32.s:
śrutvā kumāravacanaṃ bhagavānmaharṣe kṛtvā matiṃ svahṛdaye guhamāha śakraḥ /
matto bhavān na matimān vadase kimarthaṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇuṣva hariṇā gaditaṃ hi pūrvam //
naikasyārthe bahūn hanyāditi śāstreṣu niścayaḥ /
ekaṃ hanyād bahubhyor'the na pāpī tena jāyate /
//
32.d:
श्रुत्वा कुमारवचनं भगवान्महर्षे कृत्वा मतिं स्वहृदये गुहमाह शक्रः ।
मत्तो भवान् न मतिमान् वदसे किमर्थं वाक्यं शृणुष्व हरिणा गदितं हि पूर्वम् ॥
नैकस्यार्थे बहून् हन्यादिति शास्त्रेषु निश्चयः ।
एकं हन्याद् बहुभ्योर्ऽथे न पापी तेन जायते ।
॥
32.m:
Hearing Kumāra's words, O great sage, the venerable Śakra, making up his mind in his heart, said to Guha: / “You are not wiser than me; why do you speak so? Hear the words spoken earlier by Hari:

‘One should not slay many for the sake of one: this is the conclusion in the scriptures. / One may slay one for the sake of many; one does not become sinful by that.’

32.s:
32.95 etacchrutvā mayā pūrvaṃ samayasthena cāgnija /
nihato namuciḥ pūrvaṃ sodaro 'pi mamānujaḥ //
32.d:
32.95 एतच्छ्रुत्वा मया पूर्वं समयस्थेन चाग्निज ।
निहतो नमुचिः पूर्वं सोदरो ऽपि ममानुजः ॥
32.m: 32.95 Having heard this earlier, O fire-born one, while bound by an agreement, / I formerly slew Namuci, even though he was my uterine younger brother.

32.s:
tasmāt bahūnāmarthāya sakroñcaṃ mahiṣāsuram /
ghātayasva parākramya śaktyā pāvakadattayā //
32.d:
तस्मात् बहूनामर्थाय सक्रोञ्चं महिषासुरम् ।
घातयस्व पराक्रम्य शक्त्या पावकदत्तया ॥
32.m: Therefore, for the sake of many, displaying your valor, / slay the asura Mahiṣa along with Krauñca with the spear given by the Fire-god!”

32.s:
purandaravacaḥ śrutvā krodhādāraktalocanaḥ /
kumāraḥ prāha vacanaṃ kampamānaḥ śatakratum //
32.d:
पुरन्दरवचः श्रुत्वा क्रोधादारक्तलोचनः ।
कुमारः प्राह वचनं कम्पमानः शतक्रतुम् ॥
32.m: Hearing the words of Purandara, his eyes reddening with rage, / Kumāra, trembling, addressed words to Śatakratu:

32.s:
mūḍha kiṃ te balaṃ bāhvoḥ śārīraṃ cāpi vṛtrahan /
yenādhikṣipase māṃ tvaṃ dhruvaṃ na matimānasi //
32.d:
मूढ किं ते बलं बाह्वोः शारीरं चापि वृत्रहन् ।
येनाधिक्षिपसे मां त्वं ध्रुवं न मतिमानसि ॥
32.m: “Fool, what is the bodily strength of your arms, O slayer of Vṛtra, / by which you insult me? Surely you have no intelligence!”

32.s:
tamuvāca sahasrākṣastvatto 'haṃ balavān guha /
taṃ gṛhaḥ prāha ehyehi yuddhyasva balavān yadi //
32.d:
तमुवाच सहस्राक्षस्त्वत्तो ऽहं बलवान् गुह ।
तं गृहः प्राह एह्येहि युद्ध्यस्व बलवान् यदि ॥
32.m: The thousand-eyed one said to him: “I am stronger than you, Guha.” / Guha said to him: “Come, come, fight if you are stronger!”

32.s:
śakraḥ prāhātha balavān jñāyate kṛttikāsuta /
pradakṣiṇaṃ śīghrataraṃ yaḥ kuryāt krauñcameva hi //
32.d:
शक्रः प्राहाथ बलवान् ज्ञायते कृत्तिकासुत ।
प्रदक्षिणं शीघ्रतरं यः कुर्यात् क्रौञ्चमेव हि ॥
32.m: Then Śakra said: “It will be known who is stronger, O son of the Kṛttikās: / he who circumambulates Krauñca more swiftly!”

32.s:
śrutvā tadvacanaṃ skando mayūraṃ prohya vegavān /
pradakṣiṇaṃ pādacārī karttu tūrṇataro 'byagāt //
32.d:
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं स्कन्दो मयूरं प्रोह्य वेगवान् ।
प्रदक्षिणं पादचारी कर्त्तु तूर्णतरो ऽब्यगात् ॥
32.m: Hearing his words, the swift Skanda, abandoning his peacock, / set off on foot even more swiftly to perform the circumambulation.

32.s:
śakro 'vatīrya nāgendrāt pādenātha pradakṣiṇam /
kṛtvā tasthauguho 'bhyetya mūḍhaṅkiṃ saṃsthito bhavān //
32.d:
शक्रो ऽवतीर्य नागेन्द्रात् पादेनाथ प्रदक्षिणम् ।
कृत्वा तस्थौगुहो ऽभ्येत्य मूढङ्किं संस्थितो भवान् ॥
32.m: Śakra descended from the lord of elephants, circumambulated on foot, / and stood there. Guha approached [and said]: “Fool, why are you standing here?”

32.s:
tamindraḥ prāha kauṭilyaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ pradakṣiṇaḥ /
kṛto 'sya na tvayā pūrvaṃ kumāraḥ śakramabravīt //
32.d:
तमिन्द्रः प्राह कौटिल्यं मया पूर्वं प्रदक्षिणः ।
कृतो ऽस्य न त्वया पूर्वं कुमारः शक्रमब्रवीत् ॥
32.m: Indra said to him: “O tricky one, the circumambulation of this [mountain] was completed first by me, / not by you first.” Kumāra spoke to Śakra.

32.s:
mayā pūrvaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ vivadanatau parasparam /
prāpyocaturmaheśāya brahmaṇe mādhavāya ca //
32.d:
मया पूर्वं मया पूर्वं विवदनतौ परस्परम् ।
प्राप्योचतुर्महेशाय ब्रह्मणे माधवाय च ॥
32.m: Disputing with each other, “By me first!”, “By me first!”, / they approached and spoke to Maheśa, Brahmā, and Mādhava.

32.s:
athovāca hariḥ skandaṃ praṣṭumarhasi parvatam /
yo 'yaṃ vacakṣyati pūrvaṃ krauñcamabhyetya pāvakiḥ /
papracchādrimidaṃ kena kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ pradakṣiṇam //
32.d:
अथोवाच हरिः स्कन्दं प्रष्टुमर्हसि पर्वतम् ।
यो ऽयं वचक्ष्यति पूर्वं क्रौञ्चमभ्येत्य पावकिः ।
पप्रच्छाद्रिमिदं केन कृतं पूर्वं प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
32.m: Then Hari said to Skanda: “You ought to ask the mountain; / he will declare who was first.” Approaching Krauñca, the son of the Fire-god / asked the mountain: “By whom was the circumambulation performed first?”

32.s:
tanmādhavavacaḥ śrutvā krauñcamabhyetya pāvakiḥ /
papracchādrimidaṃ kena kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ pradakṣiṇam //
32.d:
तन्माधववचः श्रुत्वा क्रौञ्चमभ्येत्य पावकिः ।
पप्रच्छाद्रिमिदं केन कृतं पूर्वं प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
32.m: Hearing those words of Mādhava, the son of the Fire-god approached Krauñca / and asked the mountain: “By whom was the circumambulation performed first?”

32.s:
ityevamuktaḥ krauñcastu prāha pūrvaṃ mahāmatiḥ /
cakāra gotrabhit paścāttvāyā kṛtamatho guha //
32.d:
इत्येवमुक्तः क्रौञ्चस्तु प्राह पूर्वं महामतिः ।
चकार गोत्रभित् पश्चात्त्वाया कृतमथो गुह ॥
32.m: Thus addressed, the Krauñca, of great intelligence, said: / “The breaker of mountains did it first; afterward it was done by you, O Guha.”

32.s:
evaṃ bruvantaṃ krauñcaṃ sa krodhātprasphuritādharaḥ /
